962.skill_description: At the end of each session, clarify the homework for the week, specifying concrete exercise tasks (such as a three-column form, a five-column form, and behavioral coping training) based on the discussion points and real-life needs of the current session, explain the goals and methods, encourage active practice and application in real-life situations, transforming session content into post-session practice.
962.when_to_use: At the end of each session, when needing to convert gains into post-session practice.
962.trigger: The technique has been explained or practiced; core themes and goals are clear; the client has understood the relevant concepts/techniques and indicated willingness to try homework.

852.skill_name: Set homework check-in and follow-up arrangements
852.skill_description: When assigning homework, clarify when the next check-in will occur, agree on the sharing method and time; follow up on the execution level in the next session, providing encouragement and adjustments based on compliance; check and briefly discuss records and exercise materials at the end, reinforcing effective practices and helping the client transition from passive execution to active completion and maintenance of change.
852.when_to_use: At every closing stage during continuous sessions; simultaneously explain the check-in arrangement when assigning homework; or when reviewing homework records and practice experiences before each session.
852.trigger: Unstable homework completion by the client; need to establish a fixed rhythm for practice and feedback; when the client brings or verbally reports homework records and practice experiences.

1089.skill_name: Arrange daily relaxation exercises and record effects
1089.skill_description: After guiding relaxation training, incorporate daily practice (such as breathing/muscle relaxation) into homework, emphasizing the importance of practicing from the consultation room to daily, repeated practice; require recording subjective feelings, progress, and effects after each exercise (can use a daily form supervised by parents), to reduce anxiety and somatic tension, improve sleep, and provide basis for next check-in and adjustment.
1089.when_to_use: At the end of a session after demonstrating or teaching relaxation training as daily homework; or when confirming the details of homework, need to specify frequency and implement into daily arrangements.
1089.trigger: The client presents physical and mental reactions such as anxiety, tension, difficulty sleeping, and is willing to practice; relaxation has been practiced in the consultation room but a daily plan has not been formed.

1133.skill_description: Introduce and assign a record assignment: record daily specific situations, the automatic thoughts and emotional intensity at that time, and can include rational responses and percentage ratings after the response; encourage precise recording when conflicts occur, with parental supervision if necessary, to enhance the grasp of the situation–emotion–thought chain and use it as material for subsequent interventions.
1133.when_to_use: In the initial 1–3 sessions or in the stage requiring systematic practice, clearly define the assignment and method before the end of the session; after discussions on automatic thoughts or during the cognitive intervention phase when improving interpersonal conflict is needed.
1133.trigger: Client has difficulty noticing the relationship between automatic thoughts and emotions, emotional distress is recurrent; interpersonal conflicts occur and recalling details is difficult; cognitive pathways are understood and willing to cooperate with self-recording.

1087.skill_name: Assignment for Identifying and Analyzing Irrational Beliefs and Causes
1087.skill_description: Require systematic sorting of irrational beliefs and the resulting emotional and behavioral outcomes, write down result C and thought B around event A from personal experience, analyze the irrational component in B; record relevant evidence and the emergence of alternative thoughts, and sort and analyze other conflict-inducing events, providing material and thecontext/framework for future discussion and debate to correct.
1087.when_to_use: Before the end of the session, complete after psychoeducation on ABC or irrational belief identification, as cognitive preparation homework.
1087.trigger: Multiple irrational beliefs have been identified (e.g., absolutization, catastrophizing), the client can recall personal events and is willing to continue exploration; emotional improvement is limited and the framework needs consolidation.

892.skill_name: Assignment for Debating and Consolidating Irrational Beliefs
892.skill_description: Arrange a written debate on irrational beliefs after the session (e.g., write ≥500 words weekly), list the original irrational beliefs and newly formed rational beliefs side-by-side for comparison; complete a rational self-analysis report, provide feedback on completion on time, continuously reflect and consolidate alternative beliefs to promote internalization and generalization.
892.when_to_use: In the realization and mastery stage or after sessions on irrational belief debate techniques, used for consolidation and systematic practice.
892.trigger: Client can identify or debate some irrational beliefs in sessions and is willing to practice correction; alternative beliefs have formed but stability is insufficient.

1011.skill_name: Teaching and Assigning Thought Record/Three-Column Form Practice
1011.skill_description: Conduct psychoeducation and demonstration, explain CBT cognitive models and how to fill out the thought record; require using the thought record/three-column form/five-column form to record events, automatic thoughts, supporting and opposing evidence, and emotion ratings when mood changes or worsens, practice self-rebuttal and re-evaluation, as weekly homework to bring back for discussion and correction.
1011.when_to_use: Assign specific practice before the end of the session after explaining and demonstrating CBT principles; for the 2nd–3rd sessions or during the period of identifying and evaluating automatic thoughts, assign as weekly practice.
1011.trigger: Negative automatic thoughts appear and basic usage of the record form has been learned; can preliminarily identify emotions and automatic thoughts and is willing to practice; when evidence testing is needed.

860.skill_name: Breathing Relaxation Daily Practice and Application Scenarios
860.skill_description: The goal is to improve sleep and anxiety. Practice abdominal/slow breathing and full-body muscle relaxation before sleep and in situations involving high stress, insomnia, difficulty concentrating, fear, or palpitations. Require daily practice and recording completion and emotional changes, to provide feedback on the next session, to gradually form self-regulation skills that can be quickly applied when needed.
860.when_to_use: Implement as homework after teaching breathing relaxation techniques and before the session ends; assess during assessment and relationship building stages or at the end of sessions 3–5 when there are somatic manifestations related to sleep and anxiety.
860.trigger: Symptoms such as inability to sleep for the past month, easy waking, tension; high stress, intermittent insomnia, inability to concentrate, or frequent fear/tension; when basic methods have been learned in the session and the response is good.

853.skill_name: Administer and Interpret SCL-90/SAS/SDS to Quantify Mood
853.skill_description: Administer and interpret scales such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS during the initial interview and stage assessments to quantify anxiety, depression, and overall symptom levels. Record scores and standard scores and compare with previous or normative data; combine with clinical interview and DSM-5 screening when necessary to form objective baseline and preliminary judgments, assisting subsequent interventions and efficacy evaluation.
853.when_to_use: Initial assessment, when quickly grasping the severity of emotions is needed at the start of a session, or at key points such as stage reassessment or closing follow-up.
853.trigger: Client reports distress such as anxiety/depression, sleep disturbance, functional decline; or when objective quantification and comparison of before and after changes are required.

1191.skill_name: Use SAS/SDS to Assess and Provide Feedback with Stage Comparison
1191.skill_description: Administer the SAS and SDS scales during counseling to quantify anxiety and depression levels, record standard scores, and provide feedback and explanation to the client. Re-administer and compare changes in subsequent sessions to determine mood improvement and counseling efficacy, to serve as a basis for discussion and plan adjustment.
1191.when_to_use: Quantify emotional severity during initial diagnosis; to assess the effectiveness of interventions at stage or before termination.
1191.trigger: Client reports feelings of tension and unease, restlessness, persistent insomnia, or significant changes in mood and behavior; or when objective comparison with previous results is needed.

961.skill_name: Guide Self-Rating and Collect Others' Reports to Assess Mood Trends
961.skill_description: Invite the client to self-rate the intensity of negative emotions using scores, and compare with set goals or previous scores; simultaneously collect observations from others, such as peers, and the client's subjective reports, re-administer the scale, and comprehensively judge mood changes and efficacy, to enhance the reliability and ecological validity of the assessment.
961.when_to_use: During stage assessments or session summaries, when it is necessary to judge the extent of emotional improvement and goal attainment; during follow-up periods to verify scale changes and functional improvement.
961.trigger: Client mentions emotional fluctuations, reported improvement/worsening, or needs to review progress and assess efficacy.

1009.skill_name: Observe and Structured Inquiry for Comprehensive Assessment of Current Mood
1009.skill_description: Observe non-verbal cues such as demeanor, emotion, and tone at the start of the session, and conduct structured inquiries and documentation around insomnia, anxiety, easy crying, etc.; combine chief complaints, others' reports, and functional impairment to clarify current primary emotions and their impact, forming a comprehensive judgment of the current mood and risk.
1009.when_to_use: For status assessment and symptom tracking at the beginning of each session, or when updating mood and symptom information.
1009.trigger: Client exhibits tension, unease, or low mood, or reports emotional distress in the last two weeks, impact on sleep/learning function; teacher or family provides recent change information.

844.skill_name: Check Mood Rating and Name Emotion During Each Session
844.skill_description: Conduct a mood check at the start of the session, invite the client to review feelings from the past week or recent time, self-rate intensity of tension/anxiety using a 0–10 scale or score, record the value for subsequent comparison, and provide emotion word options to prompt them to name the emotion, quickly grasp the current baseline and fluctuations.
844.when_to_use: At the start of every session, to quickly understand the current mood and establish or update a common reference.
844.trigger: Start of a new week of sessions or client expresses vague feelings about their current mood, reports mood fluctuations, requiring scores and emotion words to describe the state.

931.skill_name: Explain Assessment Rationale and Administer Core Scales to Establish Baseline
931.skill_description: After explaining the reason for the assessment and obtaining consent from the client, administer core scales such as SCL-90, SDS, SAS, and SBQ-R, to quantify depression, anxiety, and suicide risk, obtain a baseline, and re-measure in subsequent stages to monitor changes, providing a basis for referral and intervention decisions.
931.when_to_use: In the initial assessment phase and when monitoring treatment efficacy or risk changes, especially when suicidal ideation or significant emotional distress appears.
931.trigger: Client's recent suicidal/self-harm ideation, reports worsening low mood and anxiety, or before developing a plan with psychiatry.

1088.skill_name: Opening Description and Rating of Current Emotion, Observation, and Clarification of Reactions
1088.skill_description: Guide the client to describe recent emotional reactions such as stress, anxiety, and low mood at the beginning of the session, provide normalizing understanding; guide them to grade the intensity of distress and match it with coping skills; collect mood information through non-verbal and verbal cues in the session, recall and document emotions and thoughts from the past month when necessary, ask open-ended questions about triggers and changes, clarify emotional reactions around event details.
1088.when_to_use: At the beginning of the 2nd and subsequent sessions to understand mood and stress levels, or to quickly establish the current emotional baseline before entering the topic/cognitive processing.
1088.trigger: Client recounts real difficulties and emotional distress, shows obvious emotional reactions or sighs; expresses "I don't know how to handle these thoughts".

1078.skill_name: Guide 0–10/0–100 Self-rating Anxiety and Track Before-After
1078.skill_description: Guide the client to use a numerical scale to immediately assess current anxiety/tension intensity (e.g., 0–10 or 0–100), record the score, and continuously compare it across sessions to serve as a simple indicator for grasping mood fluctuations and intervention effectiveness; can be used to score specific situations to monitor trends.
1078.when_to_use: To quickly grasp the mood at the beginning of a session, or when reviewing changes in action plans and at the end stage.
1078.trigger: Appearance of tension signs such as sweaty palms or the client reports anxiety, or reports of mood fluctuations, requiring immediate assessment and comparison with the previous score.

1143.skill_name: Stage Assessment and Comparison of Anxiety Scale Scores
1143.skill_description: Administer anxiety scales such as SAS in the initial session, and administer them again later (e.g., test anxiety scale) to quantify current anxiety levels and change trends, record scores, and perform stage-by-stage comparisons to provide a basis for intervention and outcome evaluation.
1143.when_to_use: Initial session and stage assessments; at the start of each session to understand anxiety levels or when re-testing after intervention.
1143.trigger: Client reports anxiety fluctuations, changes in sleep or function, or when a quantitative assessment of stage outcomes is needed.

1071.skill_name: Observe Non-verbal and Behavioral Cues for Rapid Mood Assessment
1071.skill_description: Pay attention to non-verbal and verbal cues such as facial expression, posture, tone of voice, speaking rate, crying, etc., such as worried facial expressions, restlessness, repetitive small movements, to comprehensively judge the current mood and level of distress; and cross-reference with scales and self-report to serve as a basis for immediate emotional assessment.
1071.when_to_use: Quick emotional scan at the beginning of each session, or when scales are unavailable; when emotional fluctuations are significant during narration.
1071.trigger: Manifest signals such as a haggard face, looking down, low tone of voice, repeated sighs, avoiding eye contact, or crying.

967.skill_name: Administer SCL-90/SAS/SDS to Establish Mood Baseline and Compare Before-and-After
967.skill_description: Use SCL-90, SAS, or SDS for assessment in the initial or assessment phase, record total scores, factor scores, and standard scores to quantify levels of depression, anxiety, and overall symptoms; re-test at the end or key points and compare with the initial test to judge mood changes and therapeutic effectiveness, serving as a basis for diagnosis and goal setting.
967.when_to_use: When preliminary psychological assessment is needed during the first interview or diagnostic assessment; when quantifying changes at the end or stage assessments.
967.trigger: Client's first visit or self-report of distress such as low mood, anxiety, insomnia, interpersonal sensitivity, requiring objective clarification of severity and comparison of before-and-after changes.

1066.skill_name: Use 0–10/0–100 emotion scale to assess intensity and track
1066.skill_description: Guide the client to rate negative emotions such as panic, restlessness, anger, sadness using a 0–10 or 0–100 emotion scale, record the score, and compare it with the previous record to quickly grasp severity and trends, as a basis for monitoring and subsequent intervention.
1066.when_to_use: During the initial mood check at the start of the session, or when quickly grasping intensity is needed after symptom fluctuations or crisis events; after exposure exercises to compare changes.
1066.trigger: Client reports negative emotions such as anxiety, irritability, depression, or difficulty describing intensity; after completing exposure exercises.

1020.skill_name: Administer SAS/SDS and provide feedback and explanation, compare at stages
1020.skill_description: After completing the SAS/SDS assessment, provide feedback to the client on the scores and their meaning, determine the severity of anxiety/depression; re-assess at initial assessment, stage assessments, and follow-up points and compare with baseline, objectively evaluate changes and consultation effectiveness, combine with medical diagnosis when necessary.
1020.when_to_use: Provide explanation after the assessment is complete; for initial diagnosis, stage re-assessments, and to evaluate the effect of interventions before ending.
1020.trigger: Scale scores are complete and show anxiety/depression or related issues; need to compare with baseline scores to assess progress.

1154.skill_name: Clinical observation of emotional cues and overall impression
1154.skill_description: Record non-verbal and verbal expressions, emotional displays, and psychotic signs during the interview, record cues of low mood, anxiety, etc., and combine with overall impressions such as thought organization, self-awareness, and guardedness to form a preliminary judgment of the current mental state, as a basis for subsequent intervention.
1154.when_to_use: During the diagnostic assessment and relationship building phase of the initial consultation, and at any point when the current emotional state needs to be grasped.
1154.trigger: Non-verbal and verbal signals such as tension, defensiveness, fatigue, or low mood upon entering; chief complaint of poor mood but no psychotic symptoms.

916.skill_name: Use SCL-90 initial assessment and post-test comparison to evaluate changes
916.skill_description: After explaining the purpose of the assessment, complete the SCL-90, record the total score and factor scores and compare with normative data or pre-test, judge the severity and change trends of depression, anxiety, interpersonal sensitivity, etc., as objective evidence of consultation effectiveness and adjustment of subsequent plans.
916.when_to_use: For the first consultation or when objective quantification of current symptoms and mental state is needed; for stage assessments or before ending to check the effect of interventions.
916.trigger: Client states they feel very bad, worries about depression, symptoms are widespread, or subjectively feels improvement/fluctuation, needs quantification and monitoring.

1144.skill_name: Observe immediate emotions and nonverbal reactions under triggering topics
1144.skill_description: When discussing triggering topics such as exams, observe nonverbal and somatic reactions such as painful expressions, tense posture, changes in speech rate and tone, and body posture, finger biting, etc., to comprehensively judge the intensity of immediate emotions like anxiety, anger, sadness, etc., as clues for the beginning of the conversation.
1144.when_to_use: During conversation segments entering the topic or discussing stressful events, when needing to quickly grasp the intensity of immediate emotions.
1144.trigger: Obvious cues such as painful expressions, tense body posture, fluctuating speech speed, and unwillingness to make eye contact appear when discussing triggering topics.

1180.skill_name: Open-ended questioning about recent mood and distress and specifying triggers
1180.skill_description: Start the conversation with open-ended questions to understand the overall mood and most troubling issues over the last one to two weeks, further specify the inducing events and duration, allowing the visitor to freely state feelings such as loneliness, depression, low self-esteem, anxiety, and changes in sleep and appetite, to comprehensively assess the scope and intensity of the mood and distress.
1180.when_to_use: In the mood assessment stage at the beginning of the first session or each session, or when needing to update the emotional state after obtaining sleep status.
1180.trigger: The visitor is willing to express distress or actively state recent feelings; has briefly reported life changes but has not clearly stated emotional state and main worries.

1136.skill_name: Directly inquire about suicidal ideation and assess risk
1136.skill_description: Directly ask in a non-judgmental way about recent suicidal thoughts or intentions, clarifying the presence, absence, intensity, frequency, and most recent occurrence time, as a basis for safety screening and risk assessment for depressed cases or those with a history of suicidal ideation.
1136.when_to_use: Mood assessment at the beginning of each session for depressed cases or those with a history of suicidal ideation; for the first assessment or when there is a significant fluctuation in emotion.
1136.trigger: The visitor mentions feelings of low spirits, despair, or death-related statements, or there is a record indicating a history of suicidal ideation.

1010.skill_name: Comprehensive assessment of suicide risk and initiation of intervention when necessary
1010.skill_description: Assess whether suicidal thoughts or behaviors have occurred in the last three months through interviews, understand the frequency, methods, and whether they are specified (e.g., location), combined with past self-harm history and current emotional presentation to determine the crisis level; even if the visitor states no current ideation, comprehensively assess and coordinate school psychological crisis intervention to ensure safety when needed.
1010.when_to_use: For the initial visit or any time suicidal ideation is found at the beginning of a conversation, prioritize safety and risk assessment; re-evaluate when information related to self-harm appears later.
1010.trigger: The visitor states danger signals such as "life is meaningless" or "can leave without pain soon," reveals past suicide experiences, or shows fluctuating suicidal ideation and behaviors.

1091.skill_name: Use SCL-90 and SAS for assessment and face-to-face interpretation feedback
1091.skill_description: Guide the client to complete the SCL-90 and SAS tests, record scores for anxiety and somatization, and provide face-to-face feedback and explanation of factor scores and comparison with normative values, forming a preliminary analysis of problem severity and type, supporting subsequent consultation planning and goal setting.
1091.when_to_use: When conducting psychological tests during the initial consultation, or in the phase where a preliminary judgment of problem severity is needed; when understanding the client's state and symptom severity at the start of the session.
1091.trigger: First visit or when the client reports distress such as anxiety, interpersonal sensitivity, somatization, etc., requiring objective quantification of symptom levels.

1189.skill_name: Observe non-verbal and physiological signals and provide brief feedback for calibration assessment
1189.skill_description: Observe non-verbal and physiological signals such as facial and limb relaxation, posture, and speech rate, such as leg shaking, hand clutching, furrowed brows, tense neck and shoulders, red eyes, etc., provide brief feedback to calibrate and supplement subjective mood information, assisting in the immediate judgment of tension and emotional arousal levels.
1189.when_to_use: Used to verify and enrich emotional assessment after mood scoring; used to immediately grasp the state at the start of the session or when discussing stress events.
1189.trigger: Noticing consistency or inconsistency between non-verbal signals and reported emotions, or observing clear physical and verbal signals of tension when narrating a stressful event.

1021.skill_name: Re-administer SAS/SDS before termination and compare with initial assessment to evaluate improvement
1021.skill_description: Re-administer the SAS/SDS at the termination or consolidation phase, record standard scores and compare with the initial assessment results, objectively evaluate the extent of improvement in anxiety and depression and the effectiveness of the consultation, provide feedback on changes to the client and use for case closure and consolidation planning.
1021.when_to_use: Effect evaluation phase during consolidation and termination; review and summary during the third to sixth consultation or follow-up review.
1021.trigger: Preparing to end the consultation or needing to evaluate phase-specific effects, with a pre-test already completed and needing comparison with the baseline.

1057.skill_name: Strengthen strengths and positive experiences to enhance self-efficacy
1057.skill_description: Identify and affirm the client's strengths (such as curiosity, courage, hope, self-control) with specific examples; guide the recall of joyful events, and compare the emotional and functional performance when using old beliefs versus new beliefs, connecting to new choices and attempts, enhancing internal motivation, self-efficacy, and commitment to change.
1057.when_to_use: Before planning a new path, after emotional release, or after a successful experience, used to consolidate motivation, maintain change, and enhance engagement.
1057.trigger: Displaying strengths in the session while underestimating self-worth; uncertainty about the benefits of correcting beliefs or hesitation about trying new behaviors; low mood, strong sense of worthlessness.

851.skill_name: Generate alternative coping and reinforce with small steps
851.skill_description: Invite the client to envision 'what to do next time,' encourage proposing alternative solutions (such as controlling emotions, discussing with classmates for compensation), and assign feasible small steps (such as communication, exercise, journaling, relaxation exercises); provide positive feedback to give them a positive experience, thereby reinforcing the willingness and efficacy to try new behaviors.
851.when_to_use: When motivation is activated, the client is willing to change but does not yet have alternative strategies, or after cognitive discussion, or when assigning homework at the end of a session, to facilitate an executable plan and consolidate motivation.
851.trigger: The client realizes the old rules are unfair and is willing to try other ways; or high stress/anxiety, divided attention, doubt about change, needs positive experience support.

1156.skill_name: Deliver external validation and affirm progress to consolidate motivation
1156.skill_description: Deliver positive feedback from the therapist and others at key points, clearly point out and affirm the client's progress and new understanding, as positive reinforcement, to encourage them to continue trying new behaviors or challenge higher goals, maintaining the motivation for change and enhancing self-efficacy.
1156.when_to_use: To consolidate motivation after the first attempt or before challenging a higher difficulty, or in the later stages of reviewing practice and symptom improvement, to maintain and amplify the motivation for change.
1156.trigger: The client hesitates to continue trying, needs encouragement and confirmation; reports slight improvement, task completion, or can state specific plans and increased confidence.

929.skill_name: Connect value outcomes and formulate specific follow-up behaviors
929.skill_description: Clearly state the positive outcomes that change may bring (such as improved relationships, better sleep), invite the client to propose and detail next steps (such as apology and communication plan), transform belief change into executable goals, enhance intrinsic motivation and sense of responsibility, and test new concepts in real-life situations.
929.when_to_use: After a technical experience or debate, or when motivation is stimulated, to transform the intention to change into specific and executable follow-up plans.
929.trigger: The client wishes to improve relationships or sleep but hesitates to act; or has expressed willingness to change/proposed initial intentions, needs clarification and planning to promote execution.

1081.skill_name: Resource-oriented review and affirmation to enhance a sense of control
1081.skill_description: Review years of effort and ability, highlight successful experiences and acknowledge effort, combine summary of phased progress with positive feedback, reduce feelings of helplessness, enhance the confidence and persistence of 'I can change,' support the correction of intermediate beliefs and continued trying of new behaviors.
1081.when_to_use: When the case is hesitant about change, self-evaluates low ability, or low self-esteem, or when reinforcing the motivation for continued change at the end of training/phase consultation.
1081.trigger: Expression of helplessness such as 'I can't/I can't change,' manifestation of inferiority and helplessness; or reports improved attention, reduced anxiety needing consolidation.

1155.skill_name: Setting Gradual Goals and Creating Success Experiences with Small Tasks
1155.skill_description: Suggest setting detailed plans, starting with easy-to-complete daily small goals, and gradually increasing the task volume; set small and achievable exercises and review successes promptly, to counter old assumptions like 'poor memory' with actual progress, enhancing the motivation for correcting old beliefs and sustained action.
1155.when_to_use: When difficulty engaging in action, seeking quick fixes, and feeling overwhelmed by anxiety, or when needing to solidify and maintain change and action through success experiences after correcting related concepts.
1155.trigger: Admitting past reliance on last-minute cramming, current difficulty starting review, initiation difficulties; hesitation about change or lack of confidence in the effectiveness of techniques.

1179.skill_name: Timely Positive Reinforcement and Encouragement to Maintain Change Motivation
1179.skill_description: In session and homework feedback, promptly express gratitude, affirmation, and praise, pointing out specific progress and strengths (such as eye contact, active communication), to solidify rational beliefs and adaptive behaviors with factual praise and emotional support, enhancing self-efficacy and the desire for continued change.
1179.when_to_use: After each session and homework feedback, or in consolidation and ending phases, or when more rational statements, new adaptive behaviors, and signs of progress appear.
1179.trigger: Client completing tasks, state improvement, improvement in interpersonal interactions, or showing new behavioral signs; lack of confidence in sustained change or need for external validation.

1176.skill_name: Affirming Effort and Planning Continuous Practice Paths
1176.skill_description: In the consolidation and ending phase, summarize the outcomes, affirm the client's investment and change, explore how to adopt rational strategies such as emotional therapy, communication, and emotional expression in the future, clarify the direction for continued practice, enhance self-efficacy, and solidify commitment to new concepts and behaviors.
1176.when_to_use: In the consolidation and ending phase of sessions 9-10, or at the end of each session, used to reinforce the motivation and path for continued change.
1176.trigger: Client worry about maintaining change or fluctuating motivation, needing to be seen, encouraged, and receive a clear path forward.

875.skill_name: Using Feedback and Review to Consolidate Progress and Inspire Persistence
875.skill_description: Periodically review effective methods and specific changes (emotional, cognitive, behavioral, and social functioning), provide anticipated/quantifiable feedback and encouragement, clarify the continuing direction or extend rational thinking to other domains, enhancing the sense of gain and intrinsic motivation for continued practice.
875.when_to_use: At the end of a phase or after completing important exercises, or when assessing effects in the concluding phase, used to integrate gains, maintain, and enhance the motivation for change.
875.trigger: Client's ambiguity regarding the benefit of counseling, questioning the necessity of continued involvement, or needing to solidify confidence and a plan for continued action in the final stages.

1167.skill_name: Weighing Pros and Cons of Unreasonable vs. Reasonable Beliefs
1167.skill_description: Jointly review the emotional and life costs caused by unreasonable beliefs, and compare the positive effects brought by reasonable beliefs, clarifying their connection to consequences such as anxiety, insomnia, decreased efficiency, etc., to create a pros and cons list or comparison table exercise, highlighting the drawbacks of the old strategy and consolidating the benefits of the new thinking.
1167.when_to_use: Used after identification and initial replacement, after initial practice, or when motivation is insufficient and wavering, to enhance the willingness to change and persistence.
1167.trigger: Client wavering, returning to old thinking, or believing change is not meaningful; insufficient recognition of the benefits of change; persistent anxiety without linking it to unreasonable beliefs; believing old concepts are safer.

1033.skill_name: Presenting the Real Costs of Old Beliefs and Old Strategies
1033.skill_description: Through cost-benefit analysis and consequence questioning, point out the costs of sticking to old beliefs and old coping mechanisms (such as limited job search scope, damaged relationships, increased anxiety and stress), focus on the unfavorable consequences of the present and future, shake the attractiveness of old beliefs, and increase the motivation to correct and try new behaviors.
1033.when_to_use: During the motivational interviewing stage or when starting to change beliefs; when the willingness to change is insufficient, the old strategy is idealized, or when focusing on real costs is necessary.
1033.trigger: Client is attached to old beliefs and defends themselves with 'at least it will make me feel better'; emphasizing the benefits of old beliefs while ignoring the consequences; primarily using avoidance or appeasement while acknowledging real damage.

1055.skill_name: Debating Unreasonable Beliefs to Promote Correction
1055.skill_description: Engage in rational debate around key unreasonable beliefs, examine evidence and logic, propose exception scenarios and alternative views, and point out the negative cycle of maintaining old beliefs, allowing the client to experience the emotional and behavioral improvement brought by reasonable beliefs, enhancing the motivation for change and readiness for action.
1055.when_to_use: Used after identifying key unreasonable beliefs, in the second stage/mastery stage, or when entering the belief correction and motivation stimulation stage after psychoeducation.
1055.trigger: Appearance of absolutistic, ought-to, or rigid beliefs accompanied by anxiety and relationship tension; or persisting in old beliefs despite understanding the theory, with no significant improvement in emotion or behavior.

1018.skill_name: Weighing the Short-Term Gains of Avoidance vs. Long-Term Costs
1018.skill_description: Guide the differentiation between immediate relief from avoidance and long-term consequences (loneliness, maintaining anxiety, weakening sense of control and self-efficacy, hindering belief correction), list the role of procrastination, checking the phone, deep breathing in the cycle, highlight that the old strategy is more detrimental than beneficial, prompt them to stop retreating and try new behaviors.
1018.when_to_use: When motivation is weak or avoidance persists, or when conducting exposure plans and motivation enhancement, to clarify the meaning of giving up safe behaviors and increase the willingness to try.
1018.trigger: Admitting that avoidance brings comfort but not realizing the long-term impact; expressing avoidance tendencies such as 'just wait for it to drop' or 'doing nothing now'; defending avoidance as 'not looking at the phone is more anxious'.

1001.skill_name: Constructing Anxiety Situational Hierarchy and Starting Tasks
1001.skill_description: Collaborate with the client and parents to list all events that cause fear or anxiety, grade them according to a subjective anxiety level of 0-100 or 1-6, arrange typical situations from low to high, prioritize low-risk, controllable starting tasks, form an executable exercise list and exposure sequence, prepare for subsequent trials.
1001.when_to_use: Planning phase before behavioral experiments/exposure, when clarifying exercise goals and difficulty gradients is needed before the first implementation.
1001.trigger: Client describes multiple avoidance or tense scenarios with varying intensity; willing to try but high anxiety, or hesitant to directly enter high-difficulty situations and worried about failure.

948.skill_name: Graded Implementation of Behavioral Experiments and Assessment of Escalation
948.skill_description: Starting from low to moderate difficulty based on the constructed anxiety levels, first desensitize in imagination, then gradually attempt in reality according to situations (e.g., bus, park, mall, provincial city, high-speed rail); after completing the goal of each stage, assess the anxiety score, proceed to a higher level when below 40 or anxiety is no longer apparent, use actual results to test and correct catastrophic beliefs and avoidance behaviors.
948.when_to_use: When conducting or advancing graded behavioral experiments and exposures, to promote practice across multiple situations, verify catastrophic beliefs, and avoid overchallenging.
948.trigger: Single exposure is effective but generalization is insufficient; retreating due to directly challenging too high; listing multiple fear scenarios and long-term avoidance of going out or riding; avoidance of specific situations like employment, postgraduate exchange, sharing inner feelings, with significant anxiety.

1072.skill_description: Explain A (event) — B (belief) — C (emotion/behavior) and the ABCDE framework in plain language, demonstrate the causal chain of "event—thought—emotion," emphasize that distress is largely determined by beliefs and beliefs can be tested and modified; invite the client to restate in their own words when necessary to build a common language and sense of possibility for change.
1072.when_to_use: In the initial stages of therapy or in the psychoeducation phase before entering cognitive/debate work, to establish a common understanding and path for change.
1072.trigger: Client attributes emotions entirely to external events, or feels confused or doubts whether "beliefs can affect emotions/whether change is possible," or proactively asks about the principles of the method.

915.skill_name: Clarifying Belief Variability and Rational Testing Path
915.skill_description: Clarify that unreasonable beliefs are not fixed; they can be clarified and corrected through confrontation, analysis, evidence testing, and rational debate, gradually building more rational thought patterns, enhancing variability cognition and self-efficacy, laying the foundation for subsequent debate and practice.
915.when_to_use: In the educational phase before starting cognitive restructuring or during phase summaries, to reinforce "belief variability" and specific change paths; when the client doubts their ability to change or lacks a sense of method.
915.trigger: Client states "I am like this" or "I can't change," or does not know how to change, feels helpless and doubtful about the outcome and methods.

895.skill_name: Demonstrate reasonable alternatives and arrange consolidation practice
895.skill_description: Demonstrate reasonable statements that align better with reality to replace old beliefs (such as "everyone has flaws and strengths," "many people like me"), explain that "changing thoughts changes emotions," and agree on reviewing the new belief for about 5 minutes daily to enhance acceptance and execution.
895.when_to_use: After identifying key unreasonable beliefs and preparing for alternatives, or when the client is willing to try different views but doubts the effectiveness and methods.
895.trigger: Client admits that old beliefs cause pain, expresses statements like "maybe I am too weird/unworthy of being liked," and is willing to try but hesitant.

907.skill_name: Use case examples to explain ABC to distinguish events and beliefs
907.skill_description: Explain A (event)–B (belief)–C (emotion/behavior) in plain language, provide in-situ examples based on the current situation, and distinguish A, B, and C, clarifying that distress stems from beliefs rather than events; introduce common characteristics of unreasonable beliefs when necessary to establish a cognitive framework and common language of "changing beliefs changes outcomes."
907.when_to_use: In the psychoeducation and insight stage, before entering cognitive intervention, or when the client urgently seeks emotional relief but is unclear about the principles.
907.trigger: Client insists "it is the event that makes me this way," attributing emotions entirely to external factors, or is confused or curious about the principles and pathways of counseling methods.

1113.skill_name: Explain three types of unreasonable beliefs and case comparisons
1113.skill_description: Explain the definitions and manifestations of the three types of unreasonable beliefs: absolutist demands, overgeneralization, and catastrophic thinking. Correspond each point with the client's own words and context, helping them identify clues in daily conversation, enhancing self-identification and corrective awareness.
1113.when_to_use: After establishing the ABC framework, when preparing to identify specific types of deviations in B, or in the cognitive education stage before argumentation.
1113.trigger: Client frequently uses extreme statements such as "should/must," "worthless/certainly..." and is confused about the concept and types of "unreasonable beliefs."

1082.skill_name: Ask downward layer by layer to the core belief
1082.skill_description: Around the automatic thoughts or key situations highlighting emotions, repeatedly ask "what does this mean/what is the worst that could happen," continuously clarifying its meaning and consequences, drilling down layer by layer until fundamental judgments about the self, others, or the world emerge (such as "I am incompetent/the world is dangerous"), and connecting surface thoughts with deeper beliefs, referencing early life experiences as clues when necessary to deepen identification.
1082.when_to_use: When emotions are intense or a key theme emerges but only surface automatic thoughts are obtained; or when entering longitudinal/case conceptualization and core belief work, requiring clarification of belief levels from surface to depth.
1082.trigger: Client remains at surface thoughts after a specific event (such as "I won't do well"), accompanied by shame, guilt, anxiety, and physiological reactions; or repeatedly exhibits self-blame, self-evaluation, and fixed reaction patterns, is confused about the source, and willing to explore further.

843.skill_name: Drill down to core beliefs through Socratic questioning
843.skill_description: Capture key automatic thoughts (such as "I will be nervous," "Others will think I am strange"), using Socratic questioning with arrows pointing down to repeatedly ask "What does this mean/What is the worst that could happen?", gradually connecting attitude rules with early experiences, until core beliefs such as "I am not worthy of love/The surroundings are unsafe/I will be abandoned" are refined.
843.when_to_use: After identifying negative automatic thoughts and needing to delve into the middle/core belief stage; or when needing to quickly move from surface thoughts to root beliefs in specific interpersonal/anxiety situations.
843.trigger: Client is emotionally intense in interpersonal situations, rigid in explanations, or states "I am not worthy of love"; surface thoughts like "They are all watching me" or "I will stutter in public" appear in records or dialogue, highly sensitive to others' evaluations, and willing to accept further questioning.

1119.skill_name: Generate multiple explanations and responses through perspective-taking
1119.skill_description: When information is vague or others' intentions are unclear, guide the client to compare different reactions of others/peers to the same event, use perspective-taking questions (such as starting from the other person's, family's, or friend's standpoint) to propose more than one possible explanation, and combine with personal experience and situational clues; discuss appropriate handling methods or alternative paths when necessary, to break down single negative attribution, broaden cognitive perspective, and alleviate anxiety and self-blame.
1119.when_to_use: When the client forms a single negative explanation for social/work/family situations, evaluates automatic thoughts, or needs to expand understanding and action options.
1119.trigger: Insisting on "only one reason/conclusion" (such as "They definitely don't like me," "I am stupid"), appearing in absolute attribution, mind-reading inference, or self-blaming explanations, leading to hesitation and inaction.

1014.skill_name: Check evidence and assess the credibility of each explanation
1014.skill_description: After proposing multiple possible explanations, urge the client to find real evidence and counter-evidence for each explanation, conduct a preliminary check based on known facts and the client's statements, write in a thought record and mark the percentage of belief when necessary, discuss the rationality of each item, to reduce emotional distress caused by overgeneralization and single negative attribution.
1014.when_to_use: When identifying automatic thoughts or having generated several alternative explanations, and needing to check evidence and estimate the rationality and relative possibility of each explanation.
1014.trigger: Client always thinks negatively, repeatedly dwells on the meaning of others' words; or explains an event as a single conclusion like "abandoned/deliberately made things difficult," ignoring other possibilities.

996.skill_name: Explain attribution differences and guide alternative explanations
996.skill_description: Illustrate the subjective experience differences brought about by different attribution styles, point out possible cognitive biases; when role-swapping or discussing conflict segments, use prompts such as "What do you think she wants to express?" to prompt the client to organize narratives from the perspective of others' intentions and feelings, opening up multi-angle thinking, expanding the variety of explanations for the event.
996.when_to_use: When the client forms a single explanation for an event and cannot see others, or when role-swapping or replaying peak conflict segments to activate others' perspectives.
996.trigger: Continuously attributing events like breakups unilaterally to the other person or the outside; falling into self-centered narratives, silence, or hesitation, unable to unfold the content from others' perspectives.

1003.skill_name: Planning and Inferring Outcomes Based on Alternative Explanations
1003.skill_description: After generating multiple plausible explanations, guide the client to corresponding coping options for each possibility (such as communication explanations or shifting focus to academics/trying other companies), preliminarily estimate feasibility by referencing peer experiences, and infer the current choices and potential feelings associated with adopting different explanations, thereby alleviating catastrophic thinking, supporting decision-making and action.
1003.when_to_use: When multiple alternative explanations have been generated and the goal is to further connect to specific behavioral choices and emotional changes, or when the client equates a single event to the sole bad outcome and needs to expand possibilities to reduce anxiety.
1003.trigger: Expressing catastrophic conclusions such as "The company not keeping me = no way out" or "Only bad outcomes"; or listing 2–3 possibilities but remaining at an abstract level without connecting to specific consequences.

1044.skill_name: Establishing and Scoring a Hierarchical Exposure Checklist
1044.skill_description: Collaboratively list specific situations that are likely to induce anxiety/obsessions with the client, score each item by subjective difficulty or fear/anxiety intensity (e.g., 0–10), and sort them from low to high to form a graded task/situation table, providing a sequential execution framework for subsequent behavioral experiments, in-vivo exposure, and response prevention, reducing the risk of failure and gradually accumulating success experiences.
1044.when_to_use: In the planning phase before implementing exposure/behavioral experiments, used to clarify target situations, difficulty, and progression order.
1044.trigger: The client can identify scenarios that trigger anxiety/obsessions but finds it difficult to directly enter high-difficulty tasks, or needs to differentiate the anxiety intensity of different situations and the exercise order.

901.skill_name: Negotiating and Determining the Starting Level of First Exposure
901.skill_description: After completing the situation list and level scoring, negotiate with the client to determine the level of the first exposure, prioritizing a tolerable low to moderate difficulty as a starting point to ensure safety and controllability, lower the entry threshold, and enhance participation and persistence.
901.when_to_use: In the task selection stage before executing exposure/behavioral experiments, when determining the starting difficulty and method is required.
901.trigger: After the situation and scoring are complete, the client expresses their tolerance level for each level; or the client is fearful of high-difficulty situations but willing to try lower-difficulty exercises.

1097.skill_name: Repeating Exposure Assessment and Progressing by Standard
1097.skill_description: Arrange repeated exposure and practice within the same level situation, potentially combined with deep breathing/muscle relaxation to alleviate tension; assess subjective anxiety after each session (e.g., 0–10 or scale score), proceed to a higher level when it is reduced by about half from the initial level, drops to 3 or below, or below 40 points; if the standard is not met, continue practice or adjust, avoid skipping levels, and steadily consolidate new coping mechanisms in a safe and relaxed environment.
1097.when_to_use: After establishing the level table and completing low-level training, or after the end of each stage of practice and when assessing the effect and deciding whether to upgrade.
1097.trigger: Significant decrease in anxiety at the current level/score close to half of the initial level, drops to 3 or below, or below 40 points; the client can stably tolerate and is willing to progress; or physical reactions such as tension during exposure require relaxation support.

881.skill_name: Active Social Practice to Test Interpersonal Cognitions
881.skill_description: Under the guidance of a therapist, arrange small, realistic exercises, such as proactively greeting classmates/roommates, interacting with peers, or approaching like-minded individuals, to increase the frequency and depth of interaction, collect feedback on others' responses and self-emotional changes, to verify concerns about being "talked about/discriminated against" and the possibility of acceptance, gradually enhancing social support and sense of belonging.
881.when_to_use: During the consolidation and termination phases, or when in a new environment desiring friendship, convert rational cognitions and self-advantage awareness into concrete social behaviors to advance interpersonal improvement.
881.trigger: Client feels isolated, lacks confidence, or worries about being talked about, but is willing to try proactive contact; wishes to improve dormitory/classmate relationships, expand support circles, or observe interpersonal and emotional changes in practice.

1002.skill_name: Construct and Score Anxiety/Fear Event Hierarchy
1002.skill_description: With the client (jointly with family when necessary), sort out specific events that trigger tension, fear, or anxiety, mark them by subjective intensity on a scale of 0–100 or by grading, and sort them from weakest to strongest (e.g., on a 10-point scale or 1–6 levels), clarify practice priority and target difficulty, to provide a basis and starting point for systematic desensitization and exposure practice.
1002.when_to_use: In the preparation phase before conducting systematic desensitization or behavioral practice, to clarify target situations, intensity, and practice sequence.
1002.trigger: Client has difficulty distinguishing the most feared scenario or unclear practice priority; significant differences in tension across different situations require a graded plan.

976.skill_name: Set Stage Goals and Practice Gradually by Level
976.skill_description: Based on the established 1–6 or 10-level anxiety scale, set stage-specific goals achievable through one's own effort for each level; practice specific events from low to high in correspondence, gradually increasing difficulty to promote desensitization.
976.when_to_use: After completing the level division, enter the start and execution phase of each level's training, to clarify the goal for that session and conduct actual practice.
976.trigger: The hierarchy has been completed, need to enter actual practice and clarify the goal for this stage; or need to gradually increase difficulty according to the predetermined sequence.

1120.skill_name: Externalize and Name Old Core Beliefs and Influences
1120.skill_description: Help the client distill old beliefs using their own words, invite the voice of the old belief and the painful experiences to be expressed; clarify the core sentence structure and the emotional and behavioral consequences it brings, making it a position and argument for one side of the dialogue, to pave the way for later refutation and replacement.
1120.when_to_use: Entering the core belief evaluation, before entering belief dialogue, or during preparation for confrontation, to focus on the old belief and clarify its scope.
1120.trigger: Client repeatedly self-negates, tying outcomes to self-worth; stating absolute thoughts like "disappointing others" or "not being loved" causes significant distress; or starting to be willing to share painful experiences and worries.

1041.skill_name: Construct and verbalize new beliefs in response to old beliefs
1041.skill_description: Guide the formation of more realistic, supportive self-statements, respond to old beliefs item by item using first-person positive phrasing, compare the impact of both on emotions and behaviors with a comparison list; record and review current positive experiences and situational evidence to prompt action based on the new belief, increase belief and solidify it into repeatable scripts.
1041.when_to_use: In consultation dialogue or homework review, when the client has shown a more realistic view and willingness to explore alternative beliefs, or during the later stages and consolidation phase of belief work when increasing the stability of the new belief is needed.
1041.trigger: Statements of self-denial or ignoring success experiences; recurrence of old thoughts (such as "I am stupid") and wavering between new and old statements; or the appearance of new cognitive signs such as "lower expectations" or "look at things from multiple angles".

878.skill_name: Guide future self to self-dialogue with a friend's perspective
878.skill_description: Have the client verbally or in writing present views and encouragement to "future confident self" regarding "current self," or transform reasonable comfort to a friend into supportive statements for oneself, prompting an internal dialogue between the supportive "new self" and the critical "old self," using new experiences to support new beliefs and correct old interpretations.
878.when_to_use: In the summary and consolidation or core belief evaluation stage, when the persuasiveness of the new belief needs to be increased and change consolidated, or when the client finds it difficult to generate alternative thoughts and needs a gentler, supportive self-voice introduced.
878.trigger: Client reports feeling fulfilled, having a sense of accomplishment, and expressing a desire to end consultation; or being harsh on oneself despite being able to give reasonable advice to others, appearing with negative automatic thoughts such as "they are deliberately not responding to me".

1149.skill_name: Summarize new explanations and list advantages to consolidate new beliefs
1149.skill_description: Synthesize new views formed in the dialogue, compare them item by item with old beliefs and mark key evidence and changes; invite verbal listing and writing of at least 5 personal strengths and resources, combined with verbal comparison of old negative statements and positive self-suggestions, prompting a dialogue between new and old beliefs, strengthening belief, self-efficacy, and transfer to similar situations.
1149.when_to_use: In the concluding and consolidation stage of the dialogue, or when self-evaluation is low, there is repeated self-deprecation, and specific self-dialogue is needed to initiate and internalize new beliefs.
1149.trigger: Client's recognition and emotional relief upon new views, such as "it seems like that/it's quite good"; or repeated negative self-talk, difficulty seeing strengths, and low acceptance of new views.

1074.skill_name: Debate old beliefs and generate rational alternatives
1074.skill_description: Employ debate techniques to guide listing or juxtaposing old and constructive beliefs or before-and-after beliefs, questioning the basis and logic item by item, recording old beliefs and responding with counterexamples, comparing the basis, consequences, and applicable situations of each pair of beliefs, generating specific rational statements to gradually replace irrational concepts, reducing anxiety and pessimistic emotions.
1074.when_to_use: In the dialogue segment of new and old beliefs or in the recovery and re-education consolidation stage, when irrational beliefs have been identified and need to be challenged, replaced, and consolidated; or when strong emotions accompany irrational beliefs.
1074.trigger: Admitting that old beliefs have problems but still being troubled; stating absolute beliefs such as "must/certainly" accompanied by anger, anxiety, or depression; insisting on statements such as "no future" or uncertainty about the evidence base, seeking answers.

906.skill_name: Review Homework and Progress and Reinforce Rational Beliefs
906.skill_description: Systematically review the process and outcomes of homework and behavioral attempts in subsequent sessions, review and consolidate new cognitive methods and rational concepts, highlight successful experiences, and provide clear affirmation and reinforcement feedback; guide the summary of consultation gains, connect new understanding with specific life scenarios, and adjust homework arrangements as necessary, to enhance the replacement and maintenance of irrational beliefs.
906.when_to_use: At the beginning or end of each session, during consolidation and termination phases, used to check homework, consolidate achievements, and plan the next steps.
906.trigger: Client brings in a record sheet, feedback on practice experience, or reports difficulties and improvements; emotions have improved but further consolidation and integration are needed.

960.skill_name: Train and Use Positive Self-Talk and Suggestions
960.skill_description: Encourage the use of positive self-talk/self-suggestions in daily situations to counteract irrational cognitions, practice more rational and constructive alternative statements for automatic thoughts such as "looking down on me," "not being a member of the class," or "hating myself"; simultaneously conduct thought recording and self-affirmation checklists, positive focus exercises, to enhance self-confidence, weaken feelings of inferiority and depression, reduce anxiety, and consolidate new beliefs.
960.when_to_use: During the phase of cognitive change consolidation and relapse prevention, as homework and daily practice; when experiencing emotional fluctuations or daily setbacks.
960.trigger: Thoughts of being looked down upon or excluded, or feelings of self-blame; learning, interpersonal setbacks, or worries about exam prospects.

1138.skill_name: Review Progress and Reinforce Self-Help Application
1138.skill_description: Systematically review key progress and practice experiences from previous consultations during the ending/consolidation phase, invite the client to recount consultation points, specifically affirm efforts and achievements, sort and summarize effective strategies and points to note, enhance self-efficacy and willingness to use, and prepare for daily self-help application and follow-up.
1138.when_to_use: Consolidation review before a phase or termination, ending and consolidation sessions, late-stage treatment.
1138.trigger: Need to integrate gains after multiple practices; entering the final session or phase summary, client asks about outcomes or expresses uncertainty.

1173.skill_name: Summarize Coping Strategies and Develop Relapse Prevention
1173.skill_description: Collaboratively summarize the causes of symptom/fear occurrence and maintenance with the client, summarize effective methods, clarify steps for coping with future relapses and key points for recognizing relapse signs, form a checklist for review and self-prompting, to consolidate skills and prevent relapse.
1173.when_to_use: During phase consolidation or near termination, or when needing to form a long-term self-help plan and develop subsequent self-help strategies.
1173.trigger: Symptoms have significantly improved, preparing to reduce session frequency or nearing termination; client worries about maintaining change and relapse risk.

837.skill_name: Assign and review automatic thought record practice
837.skill_description: Teach methods for filling out thought/ABC records, assign homework related to the current topic at the end of each session; require recording events—thoughts—emotions—behaviors and alternative views in daily situations, covering multiple similar situations to form continuous data; review experiences and outcomes in the next session to consolidate the application of identifying, evaluating, and rational beliefs.
837.when_to_use: Consolidation phase after automatic thought work, at the end of each session; review homework at the beginning of the next session.
837.trigger: Client is willing to practice and record in daily life, bring specific events and feelings, or needs to transfer learned material to daily situations.

912.skill_name: Review, summarize, and teach emotion regulation strategies
912.skill_description: In the consolidation phase, review the consultation process and belief changes, affirm progress, and teach strategies for scientific emotional release and seeking help from others; combine methods learned such as identifying thoughts, time planning, and behavioral testing to clarify transfer methods in learning and life, supporting long-term maintenance and self-help.
912.when_to_use: Late and ending stages of consultation, used for integration, planning subsequent self-management, and preventing recurrence.
912.trigger: Consultation is nearing its end, needs to develop maintenance plans and enhance self-regulation ability; client is concerned about maintenance effects or needs to clarify subsequent application paths.

887.skill_name: Identify support resources and develop self-help plan
887.skill_description: Collaborate with the client to list personal and environmental resources, systematically summarize 'friend and family support' and 'psychological resilience and strengths' demonstrated in consultation, and at the end, develop a plan for further self-exploration and resource support, enhancing self-regulation and independent coping, reducing dependence on consultation.
887.when_to_use: Consolidation phase and termination phase, when needing to enhance self-help ability and resource mobilization, or arrange subsequent paths.
887.trigger: Client is concerned about relapse prevention, or willing to move forward and needs resource support, entering the summary and feedback phase.

1161.skill_name: Guide and assign relaxation training for daily practice
1161.skill_description: Teach and assign relaxation training so that the client repeatedly practices in daily life to reduce tension and anxiety; consolidate and generalize based on the rating scale/session content in real situations, record practice effects when necessary, support the application of new cognitions and maintenance of emotion management.
1161.when_to_use: Consolidation phase of the session and after completing a training, when needing to transfer relaxation techniques to daily situations and consolidate emotion regulation ability.
1161.trigger: Client reports high anxiety factors, increased learning pressure, difficulty concentrating, or frequently experiencing tense situations in daily life.

1148.skill_name: Arranging daily relaxation exercises and recording
1148.skill_description: Arrange daily fixed or as-needed breathing/muscle relaxation exercises, cooperate with emotional dialogue when necessary; apply promptly when experiencing tension, insomnia, palpitations, etc., and record the changes after the exercise and subjective feelings to consolidate the skill and improve self-regulation in real-life situations.
1148.when_to_use: Consolidation phase and between sessions, to prevent emotional recurrence, increase skill automation, or when physiological anxiety reactions are evident.
1148.trigger: Agitation, tension, difficulty sleeping, poor concentration, chest tightness/palpitations, or when tracking exercise effects is needed.

953.skill_name: Developing a relapse prevention checklist and coping card
953.skill_description: Jointly develop a relapse warning and coping checklist with the client, specifying high-risk situations, relapse signs, immediate self-prompts and actionable steps, listing available tools and support resources, create a portable coping card, encourage continued practice, for daily application and maintenance of therapeutic effect.
953.when_to_use: Before termination or later in treatment, to transition to daily life and maintain therapeutic effect, to implement prevention plans.
953.trigger: Relief of core symptoms, preparation for ending consultation; client or parent worry about relapse, or signs of recurring problems.

952.skill_name: Self-refutation and rational statement daily practice
952.skill_description: For irrational/absolutist thoughts that arise, continuously engage in self-debate, distinguish evidence from inference, present counter-evidence, and generate rational self-statements; can use daily or weekly written practice and on-the-spot debate, repeated reading and internalization, to consolidate new cognitions and reduce the possibility of old patterns recurring.
952.when_to_use: Late psychological help to consolidation phase, between sessions and during phase summaries, to maintain and promote cognitive restructuring achievements.
952.trigger: Automatic thoughts of self-blame, catastrophizing, excessive worry, avoidance tendencies, or self-deprecation; end-of-day review or willingness to engage in self-practice.

1165.skill_name: Teaching breathing and muscle relaxation and contextual application
1165.skill_description: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and progressive muscle relaxation, requiring practice before sleep and during anxiety, and apply when under pressure, insomnia, or poor concentration, to relieve physiological tension, improve sleep, form contextualized self-help strategies, support the application of cognitive adjustments.
1165.when_to_use: When there is difficulty sleeping, increased physiological anxiety reactions, or functional impairment, self-regulation training and daily application are needed.
1165.trigger: Appearance of tension signals such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up easily, palpitations, body tension, inability to concentrate.

1085.skill_name: Summarize and synthesize common themes of automatic thoughts across contexts
1085.skill_description: Collect and organize automatic thoughts/emotions/behavioral records from multiple contexts (three-column tables, thought records, etc.), horizontally compare high-frequency phrases and reaction patterns, categorize by dimensions such as ability, self-worth, acceptance/being loved, and extract recurring common cores as a basis for core belief candidates.
1085.when_to_use: After completing several records or multiple sessions, when entering case conceptualization or cross-case analysis, when summarizing deeper themes from multi-context materials.
1085.trigger: Frequent expressions of self-blame, inadequacy, not being liked/excluded in different contexts, accompanied by stable negative emotions or similar reaction patterns; multiple records point to the same evaluation theme.

984.skill_name: Name common themes as core beliefs and verify
984.skill_description: After summarizing commonalities across contexts, summarize them into concise core belief phrases (e.g., "worthless," "incompetent," "not liked/unlovable"), present them in a conversational manner, and jointly verify their appropriateness with the client to form a preliminary consensus on core beliefs, incorporating them into conceptualization.
984.when_to_use: After cross-context comparison and when stable repeating themes have emerged, preparing to enter core/intermediate belief work and modification.
984.trigger: Same theme words or judgments appearing frequently in multiple records, high belief certainty or intense emotions, the client shows resonance or exhibits a clear emotional reaction to the generalized statement.

882.skill_name: Review homework and summarize recurring themes across contexts
882.skill_description: In sessions, retrieve and organize homework such as ABC/thought records, compare automatic thoughts and emotional reactions across different entries, categorize by dimensions such as ability, acceptance, self-worth, and capture recurring themes to provide a basis for extracting core beliefs.
882.when_to_use: When the client has completed record homework, when integrating materials and identifying common cores of core beliefs in sessions; or in the second to third stage of generalization and summarization.
882.trigger: Multiple comparable records appear in sessions; automatic thoughts across different events continuously revolve around similar evaluations such as "useless/can't write well/excluded" with high emotional scores.

957.skill_name: Name core beliefs and incorporate into cognitive conceptualization
957.skill_description: Directly extract the summarized recurring themes into core belief categories (e.g., "incompetent," "unlovable," "world is unsafe"), and check consistency with specific examples and current distress, forming cognitive conceptualization conclusions to guide subsequent interventions.
957.when_to_use: After summarizing automatic thought themes, when needing to clarify core beliefs and use them to set intervention goals or enter subsequent assessment.
957.trigger: Stable themes related to ability and self-worth/being recognized have been identified, and the client's social setbacks, avoidance, or low mood are highly related to them.

1045.skill_name: Cross-contextual Collection and Comparison for Automatic Thought Synthesis Core
1045.skill_description: List automatic thoughts and emotional behavioral cues from multiple daily/social scenarios (e.g., three-column tables), horizontally compare their commonalities and negative assumptions (such as being scrutinized, being denied, inadequacy, "must/should"), summarize recurring common cores, to provide a basis for subsequent restructuring.
1045.when_to_use: When performing horizontal case analysis or when preparing to summarize core themes after accumulating materials from multiple contexts.
1045.trigger: Similar worries and automatic thoughts repeatedly appear across different events, or multiple B's are highly consistent in tone and evaluation dimensions ("must", "should", "will be denied").

939.skill_name: Compare Common Cores and Name Core Belief Categories
939.skill_description: Based on cross-contextual comparison, capture high-frequency evaluation dimensions (ability, being loved/accepted, etc.), categorize ability denial statements like "I can't.../I cannot..." into themes such as "incompetence/self-underestimation," refine and name them as corresponding core belief categories, and verify with the client.
939.when_to_use: When cross-contextual automatic thoughts have been fully collected and are entering the synthesis stage, and need to be elevated to clear core belief statements.
939.trigger: Fixed views of inability, inferiority, or being judged frequently appear in multiple learning/exam or social contexts; the object of evaluation and emotional effect are consistent.

1034.skill_name: Integrate Multi-source Cross-contextual Materials for Theme Synthesis
1034.skill_description: Gather thoughts and experiences from different contexts and sources (self-report, homework, third-party feedback, growth experiences, etc.), and compare their common cores (such as not being supported, feeling isolated, being weak, pessimism about relationships), to refine recurring themes pointing to core beliefs.
1034.when_to_use: After completing multiple sessions and material collection, when needing to integrate information across classroom, family, and interpersonal interactions to identify core beliefs.
1034.trigger: Multiple sources repeatedly point to similar themes of self-worth and being loved, or stable patterns such as distrust of men, excessive comparison of rankings.

1019.skill_name: Name Candidate Core Beliefs and Verify with Distress
1019.skill_description: Name the recurring themes as candidate core beliefs (e.g., "I am unlovable," "I am incompetent"), and verify their explanatory power against the client's real distress (social setbacks, avoidance of places, emotional low mood), to confirm the validity of the identification.
1019.when_to_use: When recurring themes have been synthesized, and need to form clear core belief statements and verify their association with the problem list.
1019.trigger: Clear recurring themes have emerged, and the client's feelings of loneliness, avoidance of certain places, or self-incompetence are highly related to that theme.

1025.skill_name: Review and Categorize Repeated Cognitive Themes in Multiple Records
1025.skill_description: Systematically review and summarize weekly/multiple ABC or thought records to identify recurring points of focus and self-evaluations (such as contamination/danger, perfectionistic demands, self-blame, inadequacy), categorize them by labeling, and capture common core themes, preliminarily state potential core beliefs, and cross-reference with the client.
1025.when_to_use: During phase-based review and theme summarization after completing thought records for several weeks or multiple exposures/sessions.
1025.trigger: Repeated patterns in multiple records such as "must find a perfect explanation," "must constantly watch out for danger," or "fear of not writing well," or the client stating "always/repeatedly" thinking this.

863.skill_name: Assign ABC/ABCDE Records to Collect Material Across Contexts
863.skill_description: Arrange homework to record event A, belief B, and outcome C (and D refutation, E new effect) using the ABC or ABCDE format, requiring the marking and analysis of unreasonable components in B, recording thoughts and feelings of contradictory scenarios item by item, and collecting them for cross-sectional comparison and summarization of repeated themes.
863.when_to_use: In the psychological helping phase or after the second consultation, when systematically collecting automatic thoughts and irrational beliefs from multiple contexts in preparation for subsequent generalization.
863.trigger: Insufficient session material or the client's lack of understanding of the relationship between emotions and beliefs; or unclear themes, concluding based only on impression, requiring systematic recording of A, B, and C through homework.

838.skill_name: List and Compare Supporting and Contrary Evidence
838.skill_description: Around specific automatic thoughts, extract observable facts from recent situations, list supporting and refuting evidence separately; combine thought records, self-questioning, and continuous questioning to specify concrete details, retrieve opposing information from another perspective, point out contradictions with the original thought when necessary, balance information, correct overgeneralization, and develop more reasonable judgments.
838.when_to_use: During the evaluation/challenging of automatic thoughts phase, when the client strongly believes in or experiences intense emotions related to negative thoughts, requiring factual testing of their reality and balancing information.
838.trigger: Repeated absolute conclusions such as "I can't do anything/they are deliberately targeting me," focusing only on negative details or treating assumptions as facts while ignoring contrary evidence and experiencing high emotional arousal.

936.skill_name: Rate Belief and Emotion Before and After
936.skill_description: Before and after evidence sorting, ask the client to rate their level of belief in the core automatic thought, and compare the changes in emotional intensity; compare new and old views to consolidate more reasonable alternative statements and enhance cognitive flexibility.
936.when_to_use: After listing and checking evidence, used to detect the effect of intervention and promote cognitive adjustment.
936.trigger: Specific automatic thoughts have been identified and evidence checking is complete, but the old thought persists or emotional relief is not significant.

893.skill_name: Clarify the Chain and Retrieve Counterexamples
