893.skill_description: Guide the client to recall 'when/what were you thinking/what happened after', linking the situation—thought—outcome; simultaneously retrieve counterexamples and objective facts for the same situation, point out contradictions when necessary, and invite explanations to concretize evidence, avoid conclusions based on feeling, and lay the foundation for subsequent refutation and alternative thinking.
893.when_to_use: At the beginning of the assessment or when evidence is confused; during the debate process when specific evidence needs to be concretized and verified.
893.trigger: Only giving conclusions without details, narrative jumps; inferring the whole from individual experiences, ignoring counterexamples or ignoring one's own objective factual data.

963.skill_description: Place supporting and opposing evidence side-by-side for comparison, assess which side is more substantial, restate the explanation that is more fact-based by synthesizing key information, and use brief open-ended questions to prompt the client to correct their original conclusion themselves, generating more objective alternative thoughts to alleviate emotion.
963.when_to_use: When both supporting and opposing evidence have been sufficiently collected, and information needs to be integrated to make a conclusion and form alternative thoughts.
963.trigger: The client admits a lack of evidence or shows signs of belief loosening such as hesitation or changing their mind during comparison.

1115.skill_name: Update Belief Level After Evidence Integration
1115.skill_description: After checking progress, time, and past records as evidence, help the client form a more reasonable statement and re-evaluate the level of belief in the automatic thought; compare the impact of new and old thoughts on emotions, promoting cognitive updating and a decrease in anxiety/discomfort.
1115.when_to_use: After completing evidence collection and weighing, when the conclusion needs to be transformed into new cognition and belief level/emotional changes need to be observed.
1115.trigger: Maintaining the old thought or lack of noticeable emotional relief even after listing evidence, requiring re-evaluation to promote adjustment.

1048.skill_description: Based on 'evidence' questions, guide the client to list specific facts supporting and not supporting the automatic thought, and distinguish between thoughts and objective facts to test the truthfulness of the thought, weaken bias, and alleviate emotion, and form alternative thoughts based on this when necessary.
1048.when_to_use: In the cognitive intervention stage, when assessing automatic thoughts triggered by events, needing to check the truthfulness of the thought with facts, and preparing for alternative thoughts.
1048.trigger: Declarative thoughts under intense emotion (e.g., 'You abandoned me') or dysfunctional self-blame evaluations, with high belief in the automatic thought.

1013.skill_description: After evidence sorting, invite the client to express alternative thoughts in their own words that are more context-specific, assign a belief percentage to them, compare them with the original thought, re-evaluate related emotions, observe a decrease to consolidate learning and guide subsequent actions.
1013.when_to_use: When it is necessary to form feasible alternative thoughts and evaluate their impact on emotions after evidence examination.
1013.trigger: When the client exhibits self-negation or clear single attribution, but is willing to try thinking from different angles, or shows signs of emotional/belief loosening.

842.skill_name: Organize Alternative Thoughts into Coping Cards
842.skill_description: Organize the listed supporting and refuting evidence and more reasonable views into consultation notes or coping cards, as alternative thought entries to be used when facing triggering situations, for consolidation and ready access.
842.when_to_use: In the stage of evaluating automatic thoughts and after alternative thoughts have been formed, this is the step for consolidation and daily use.
842.trigger: When self-evaluation is rigid, anxiety is high, and specific evidence and written tools are needed to correct views.

1054.skill_description: After analyzing a specific issue and identifying irrational beliefs, use guided questions/hypotheses/three questions, etc., to debate them, compare the reasonableness of the views, prompt the client to correct or abandon irrational concepts, alleviating shame, guilt, and anxiety.
1054.when_to_use: In the psychological help/resolution stage, or after identifying negative automatic thoughts, in the evaluation phase, when irrational beliefs need correction.
1054.trigger: Repeated statements such as 'I am not good enough/It was useless even if I said it/I must sacrifice myself'; tension, shame, guilt, anxiety arising from interpersonal conflicts or events.

1035.skill_name: Arrange Behavior and Resource Training to Accumulate Positive Evidence
1035.skill_description: Assist the client to clarify career direction and executable learning goals (e.g., postgraduate entrance examination), set up and practice problem-solving and behavioral coping homework, recommend books and exercises relevant to the theme, notice and reinforce strengths and positive resources, gain positive feedback in real-life situations, provide actual evidence for alternative negative beliefs and enhance self-efficacy and functioning.
1035.when_to_use: In the stage of automatic thought adjustment, preparation for core belief work, or parallel progression, or when emotions are relatively stable and positive evidence supporting the new narrative needs to be accumulated in daily life.
1035.trigger: When the client focuses on learning/employment and is willing to set specific goals; when cognitive adjustments need to be translated into behavior, enhancing self-efficacy; when willing to try reading and practicing, or showing interest in their own strengths.

897.skill_name: Generate and reinforce reasonable core beliefs to replace
897.skill_description: Collaboratively form more realistic core beliefs with the client based on objective facts and supporting evidence (e.g., "I have strengths," "Many people like me"), used to replace old unreasonable beliefs, and reinforced in subsequent work.
897.when_to_use: When entering the cognitive restructuring phase after identifying and analyzing the unreasonableness of core beliefs.
897.trigger: The client can clearly state negative core beliefs and is willing to try new perspectives and expressions.

908.skill_name: Review, consolidate, and generalize new beliefs
908.skill_description: In the consolidation and ending phase, guide the client to review gains, continuously compare new and old beliefs, and collect positive evidence, transfer them to learning and life situations, rehearse coping strategies for future difficulties, stabilize the change, and prevent relapse.
908.when_to_use: In the consolidation and ending phase, when preparing to transfer the technique to daily life or when more reasonable views have been formed.
908.trigger: After completing homework reflection and having formed more reasonable views; early signals of wanting to maintain change or the recurrence of old thoughts.

1077.skill_name: Develop behavioral goals and simulate tasks to test new beliefs
1077.skill_description: Collaboratively develop clear, actionable behavioral goals and practice plans, assign tasks such as completing simulations with a formal mindset and self-assessment, use the process and results as real evidence, correct failure predictions, enhance self-efficacy, and consolidate cognitive and behavioral change.
1077.when_to_use: In the consolidation phase when behavioral results are needed to support cognitive change and enhance self-efficacy, or when the consultation later aims to transform new beliefs into stable behavioral patterns.
1077.trigger: The client lacks confidence in their abilities or doubts their actual performance; feedback improves and expresses a willingness to continue trying.

902.skill_name: Establish and strengthen new rational concepts
902.skill_description: Assist the client in forming new reasonable concepts, use reasonable concepts to replace unreasonable thought patterns, reduce the vicious cycle of negative emotions, and enhance cognitive resources and self-regulation ability for coping with anxiety.
902.when_to_use: When entering the belief replacement and consolidation phase after disputing unreasonable beliefs.
902.trigger: The client has admitted the original belief is unreasonable and is willing to try new perspectives and explanatory frameworks.

1110.skill_name: Questioning examples and self-review to identify unreasonable beliefs
1110.skill_description: Through questioning and guiding self-review, ask the client to provide recent specific situations and thoughts, notice absolutistic unreasonable beliefs such as black-and-white thinking, clarify their connection to current emotions, to provide material for subsequent correction and reconstruction.
1110.when_to_use: After establishing the work framework/around the third session, entering the belief identification stage, when extracting changing concepts from specific events.
1110.trigger: Client expresses self/professional evaluation with absolutistic, devaluing statements accompanied by strong emotions, or when suffering from mixed negative beliefs, difficult to self-clarify.

1187.skill_name: Review and higher-intensity reality testing in the ending phase
1187.skill_description: In the ending phase, review coping methods and newly formed rational beliefs, encourage attempting higher-intensity exposure and response blocking in a safe environment, complete new reality testing, to enhance confidence and replace old beliefs.
1187.when_to_use: At the end of counseling or in phase summaries, when consolidating results and enhancing self-efficacy.
1187.trigger: Client's symptoms have significantly improved, expresses hope to further consolidate and challenge more difficult situations.

943.skill_name: Review, consolidation, and relapse prevention education
943.skill_description: Systematically review the change process and effective strategies in the later stages of counseling, invite the client to self-summarize and provide suggestions for continued practice, provide psychoeducation for relapse prevention, plan future challenges and daily transitions, cultivate independent problem-solving ability, promote generalization and maintenance of new beliefs in life.
943.when_to_use: Later stages of counseling/ending phase, when goals are largely achieved, when solidifying results, formulating follow-up self-help plans and relapse prevention.
943.trigger: Behavioral improvement and emotional stability have been sustained, entering the 9th–10th session or nearing the end; the client needs to maintain and promote change and prepare to end counseling.

1196.skill_name: Debating unreasonable beliefs and replacing with rational concepts
1196.skill_description: Based on the client's acceptance of theory and analysis, use specific cases to point out that absolutistic demands cause distress rather than the event itself, use dialectical method for logical and evidence testing, guide replacing unreasonable beliefs with more rational evaluations, reinforce new cognitions such as 'controllable is thought', improve emotions and promote learning and interpersonal adaptation.
1196.when_to_use: After refutation, entering cognitive reconstruction or the third and fourth stages of breakthrough, for replacing identified irrational concepts.
1196.trigger: Client adheres to absolutistic, overgeneralization, or catastrophic beliefs, accompanied by strong emotions such as anxiety/shame or functional impairment, and is willing to try to change beliefs.

925.skill_name: Applying ABC identification and belief modification in homework
925.skill_description: Assign and supervise homework, record A (antecedent event), B (belief), C (emotion/behavior), identify unreasonable B and generate causes and reasonable alternatives, continuously practice identification and modification to consolidate cognitive change and emotional improvement in the session.
925.when_to_use: Application phase between sessions, or when preliminary ABC understanding is achieved and entering the belief replacement and consolidation phase.
925.trigger: Client reports recent events and emotional fluctuations, or understands ABC but is still troubled by unreasonable beliefs and is willing to record and practice.

977.skill_description: Explain the principles of REBT and ABC to the client, demonstrate attributing emotions to beliefs rather than events, organize and locate unreasonable beliefs by sorting A-B-C around the current distress, arrange multiple practices until natural use is possible, laying the foundation for subsequent debate and modification.
977.when_to_use: Insight phase initiation or when the second and subsequent consultations enter cognitive application training, used to specify problems and locate beliefs to be modified.
977.trigger: Client is confused about the cause of problems, attributes all emotions to external events while ignoring the role of beliefs, or has a preliminary understanding of ABC but finds it difficult to use independently.

968.skill_name: Consolidation phase review, affirmation, and promotion of transfer
968.skill_description: Summarize the core of the previous changes, specifically praise and affirm progress, review scales and subjective improvements, reinforce education and reasonable beliefs, encourage self-acceptance and proactive interpersonal relationships, continuously apply what has been learned to learning and life, prepare for termination and self-management.
968.when_to_use: Consolidation and termination phases, used to solidify new beliefs and behaviors, integrate and transfer, and prepare for ending.
968.trigger: Symptoms have significantly improved, scales and subjective scores have decreased, client is in good condition and expresses a willingness to continue making efforts.

1008.skill_name: Assign structured homework to consolidate new beliefs
1008.skill_description: Arrange completion of 'reasonable self-analysis report', core belief homework sheet, written rewriting and comparison of unreasonable/reasonable beliefs, record antecedent events, debate process, and emotional changes, provide timely feedback on practice and effects, promote the transfer and internalization of belief restructuring.
1008.when_to_use: After debate techniques or after each psychological help phase, when new beliefs are preliminarily formed or at the end of a phase consultation.
1008.trigger: Belief debate is completed and reasonable alternatives are preliminarily formed but stability is insufficient, or is willing to continue writing and practicing outside of sessions.

1062.skill_name: Design and implement behavioral experiments to test new beliefs
1062.skill_description: Design small, feasible tasks in interpersonal and learning contexts close to daily life, specify evidence collection methods, test new and old beliefs in real situations; guide timely help-seeking when necessary and reinforce help-seeking behavior, using real-world feedback to reinforce the control of alternative beliefs and reduce the control of old beliefs.
1062.when_to_use: When a new belief has been proposed and is preliminarily accepted, and real testing and reinforcement are needed, or when the old belief still holds the advantage.
1062.trigger: Client verbally agrees with the new belief but lacks behavioral evidence, is unsure, avoids seeking help, or worries about the real effects.

1169.skill_name: Use Socratic questioning to challenge old beliefs and generate alternatives
1169.skill_description: Set layered questions around core beliefs based on homework materials, collect evidence supporting/opposing, and alternative explanations; deconstruct absolutistic and overgeneralization assumptions, guide the replacement of concepts like "I am definitely unwelcome" with more balanced statements, and encourage repeated use of new formulations in similar situations.
1169.when_to_use: Entering the belief restructuring/reconstruction phase, the target belief has been identified, and the client needs to generate new perspectives.
1169.trigger: Client insists on general conclusions like "Everything is Y" or expresses them in absolute language and scores high, accompanied by strong emotions and willingness to explore alternative statements.

1060.skill_name: Apply the emotion ABC and refute to generate alternative beliefs
1060.skill_description: Use the emotion ABC framework to organize event—belief—outcome, locate unreasonable beliefs, engage in refutation, and generate more reasonable alternative beliefs, promote objective self-awareness and emotion regulation, consolidate therapeutic effectiveness.
1060.when_to_use: When an unreasonable belief is associated with negative emotions, and systematic cognitive reconstruction and consolidation are needed.
1060.trigger: Beliefs such as "It's all my fault" or "I am not loved" exist, accompanied by emotional experiences such as depression, guilt, or helplessness.

871.skill_name: Explain the ABC model to promote insight and consensus
871.skill_description: Deconstruct events into A (triggering event)—B (belief)—C (emotion/behavior), emphasize that emotions are caused by B rather than A, explain the rational emotion therapy ABC model, distinguish between cognition and fact, correct the habit of attributing reactions solely to events, explain the path for change, and unify intervention goals and language.
871.when_to_use: Before entering the belief restructuring/application phase or when first explaining the principles of therapy, used to establish a common theoretical framework and consensus.
871.trigger: Client attributes emotions entirely to external events, is confused about consulting methods and goals, or cannot distinguish between emotions and thoughts, cognition and facts.

884.skill_name: Invite and Review Task Execution and Experience
884.skill_description: Jointly review the previously assigned tasks (such as relaxation training, thought/behavior records, reading), check the completion level, frequency, and quality item by item, invite them to summarize their experiences and difficulties encountered, supplement or clarify records in the session when necessary, extract effective practices and clues, to serve as a basis for subsequent discussion and adjustments.
884.when_to_use: During the task review segment at the start of each session, or when reviewing records and effects at the end of a task cycle.
884.trigger: Client brings in a record sheet or verbally reports on exercise progress; when reviewing tasks, need to understand the execution status, experience, and effects.

1150.skill_name: Affirm Progress and Provide Reinforcement and Adjustment
1150.skill_description: During task review, give specific affirmation and encouragement for efforts and improvements, reinforce rational cognitions and positive changes in emotion/sleep, if execution fluctuates, adjust the difficulty or frequency of the task as appropriate, to consolidate motivation and effectiveness and promote continued practice.
1150.when_to_use: When discussing task content and observing progress, or when consolidating and adjusting after systematically checking completion levels.
1150.trigger: Client shows signs of identifying biases, thought adjustments, emotional reduction, or sleep improvement in the task, or when execution fluctuation requires consolidation.

879.skill_name: Check and Discuss Record and Thought Tasks
879.skill_description: At the beginning of the session, check the record-keeping tasks assigned previously (conflict/emotion records, thought records, ABC tasks, etc.), understand the completion status, the ability to identify automatic thoughts and alternative explanations, discuss experiences and questions, to serve as a basis for entering the current topic and further training.
879.when_to_use: During the task review segment at the start of the next session after assigning record/thought tasks.
879.trigger: Client brings in or verbally reports records such as "contradictory scenario + thoughts and feelings at that time," or when need to understand the extent of execution and difficulties encountered.

1052.skill_name: Report and Summarize Task Experience and Changes
1052.skill_description: Ask the client to report on the experience, emotional intensity, and interpersonal/functional changes after completing the task, follow up on new findings and cognitive changes, extract meaningful gains or troubles, to serve as a basis for subsequent consolidation and in-depth discussion.
1052.when_to_use: During task feedback discussions, when needing to present the effects and feelings brought by the task, when consolidating experiential learning.
1052.trigger: Client can talk about the reduction in stress/anxiety, attitude changes, or new insights after completing tasks such as diaries, exercise, or cognitive exercises.

1058.skill_name: Timely affirmation of progress and reinforcement of continued practice
1058.skill_description: After feedback on the assignment, promptly affirm persistence and improvements (such as attention or relationship improvement, symptom relief), summarize specific gains, reinforce self-efficacy and motivation to continue, and encourage daily sustained practice.
1058.when_to_use: At the end of each assignment review or when positive changes occur.
1058.trigger: Client demonstrates positive outcomes from the assignment, progress in practice, or increased completion rate.

1067.skill_name: Identifying and analyzing difficulties in assignment execution
1067.skill_description: During the assignment review, invite the client to describe the process and experience of execution, focusing on obstacles such as time management, avoidance, and fear, systematically analyze sticking points and negative experiences, clarify the rationale and goals of the assignment, and provide a basis for subsequent adjustments and planning.
1067.when_to_use: When assignment review shows incompleteness, unstable execution, or confusion.
1067.trigger: Client mentions obstacles such as "not enough time/don't know how to do it/unwilling to think about it," or reports poor outcomes and negative experiences.

1083.skill_name: Providing guidance and demonstration for assignment difficulties
1083.skill_description: When the client is confused about assignment steps, clarify specific difficulties and provide brief teaching and demonstration (such as self-compassion, shared humanity, present moment awareness, and alternative language), agree on feasible solutions and next steps, to reduce execution barriers.
1083.when_to_use: When the assignment is incomplete or the quality of completion is poor, and specific difficulties exist.
1083.trigger: Client provides information indicating confusion about steps or items to fill out, such as "don't know how to respond to myself."

981.skill_name: Affirming assignment gains and consolidating positive evaluations
981.skill_description: Review and reinforce the positive changes brought by the assignment, convey others' recognition, guide the client to see the positive aspects and provide specific encouragement; can continue thought recording practice and coordinate with a self-affirmation checklist to consolidate the gains from the "observing strengths" task, enhance self-esteem and motivation for continued execution.
981.when_to_use: During the assignment review phase or the concluding stage and subsequent consolidation practice.
981.trigger: Client completes tasks on time and reports results such as reduced anxiety, improved sleep, increased confidence, or still holds a negative evaluation of self-worth.

1145.skill_name: Review Records and Identify Automatic Thoughts
1145.skill_description: Review the client's records of thought/emotion events, check each item for events, automatic thoughts, emotions, and ratings, select representative key situations to help summarize thoughts in a single sentence and identify patterns, serving as an entry point for subsequent cognitive interventions.
1145.when_to_use: During homework review, after completing records of thought identification, self-observation, or thought change.
1145.trigger: Client submission or verbal report of records, with items showing significant distress or high-intensity emotions.

1181.skill_name: Review Relaxation Training Execution and Effects
1181.skill_description: Review the frequency, duration, and completion of relaxation/imagination exercises at the start of the session, check for changes in emotions and sleep, invite the client to report on their experience before and after the training, assess the effect, and decide whether to continue or adjust.
1181.when_to_use: During the homework review at the start of each session, especially for follow-up after assigning relaxation training.
1181.trigger: Client brings relaxation training records or verbally reports on the exercise status, with lingering worries or unalleviated emotions.

904.skill_name: Check and Feedback on Homework Completion and Obstacles
904.skill_description: At the start of the session, check the completion status and difficulties of the previous homework, invite on-site demonstration or practice when necessary, to verify completion through real behavior; accept honest non-completion and explore obstacles, to provide basis for subsequent discussion and adjustments.
904.when_to_use: During the homework review phase at the start of each session, especially when homework is incomplete or needs review.
904.trigger: Arrival at the scheduled review time or client bringing homework/report of execution status and difficulties.

933.skill_name: Review Cognitive Homework Comparison of Expectation and Outcome
933.skill_description: For homework such as cognitive challenge experiments, analysis/comparison and debate of irrational beliefs, review the completion status, compare expectations with actual results item by item, discuss concept alternatives and insights, assess emotional and coping effects, and summarize evidence and experience.
933.when_to_use: During the homework feedback phase of the next or subsequent session after completing relevant cognitive homework.
933.trigger: Client has completed a specific attempt with records to compare, or reports of conceptual change/persistent irrational beliefs.

974.skill_name: Check sleep and relaxation homework and reinforce feedback
974.skill_description: Check the execution (frequency, duration, and deviations) of sleep diaries, relaxation training, and daytime behaviors, review the effect based on subjective feelings and changes in sleep indicators, timely affirm progress and suggest adjustments on the spot, consolidate effective behaviors.
974.when_to_use: When reviewing the execution and effect of sleep hygiene and relaxation behaviors.
974.trigger: Client submits records or reports of extended sleep time, reduced awakenings, or adherence to training.

1147.skill_name: Follow up on relaxation meditation frequency and effect
1147.skill_description: Regarding practices such as breathing/mindfulness relaxation and emotional dialogue, inquire and verify the frequency, duration, and records of the practice, discuss experiences and obstacles, connect with improvements in anxiety and sleep, adjust prescriptions when necessary, and encourage continued daily application.
1147.when_to_use: During the homework review and skill consolidation phase at the beginning of each session.
1147.trigger: Last time requested daily practice and recording, or client feedback on practice effect/difficulty encountered, or anxiety/insomnia not alleviated.

932.skill_name: Review three-five column sheet and clarify summarization
932.skill_description: Jointly check the completeness of the records in the three-column/five-column sheet and mood ratings with the client, assess the completion level of automatic thought identification and challenging exercises, point out common confusions and provide examples for clarification, compare common points across multiple entries, and provide basis for subsequent cognitive training.
932.when_to_use: During the homework review at the start of each session, especially for weekly three/five-column sheets.
932.trigger: Client brings three/five-column sheet records, reflecting difficulty in identification or need for systematic discussion and analysis.

1015.skill_name: Emotion normalization, present acceptance, and seeking help
1015.skill_description: Normalize negative emotions, encourage the client to accept the existence and limits of emotions; when anxiety events occur during the session, guide them to bring attention back to the present, engage in non-judgmental awareness and acceptance; when self-regulation is difficult, arrange to proactively contact the psychological center or hospital for professional support to stabilize emotions and advance subsequent cognitive and behavioral work.
1015.when_to_use: When emotional intensity is high, affecting learning and life functions, or when anxiety events and emotional fluctuations occur during the session and emotional stabilization is needed first.
1015.trigger: Persistent anxiety, depression, sleep disorders, or physical symptoms (such as trembling, nausea, stomach pain, feeling unable to find peace), expression of helplessness; sudden tension from specific events making continued communication difficult.

988.skill_name: Teach and practice relaxation to stabilize emotions
988.skill_description: Demonstrate and coach actionable relaxation techniques, assign regular practice 2–3 times a day, reduce physiological arousal, alleviate restlessness, anxiety, and insomnia, serve as an auxiliary means for cognitive exploration and action planning, enhance self-emotional regulation ability.
988.when_to_use: Diagnosis or mid-stage consolidation phase, and when emotions are high, physical and mental reactions are noticeable, and rapid stabilization is needed during sessions.
988.trigger: Emotions are easily out of control, restless or poor sleep; or experiencing symptoms such as insomnia, nausea, stomach pain, inner unease, severe anxiety.

849.skill_name: Allow and guide reasonable emotional expression
849.skill_description: Provide a safe space and support (listening, interpretation, clarification), allow and encourage the expression of anxiety, sadness, fear, and conflicting emotions, promote release and burden reduction; guide the client to find and practice appropriate ways of reasonable expression, distinguish between effective and ineffective methods, and retain reproducible methods, lay the foundation for subsequent cognitive and behavioral interventions.
849.when_to_use: Accumulation of negative emotions, difficulty in calming down, or when old methods are ineffective; early stages of the client or when emotions are high and need to reduce emotional tension and build alliance.
849.trigger: Experiencing irritability, anxiety, impulsivity, or 'can't control myself'; intense emotions during discussions about family conflict that are difficult to express or are avoided; expressing experiences like 'always want to cry, feeling very bad'.

1135.skill_name: Guide emotion naming, differentiation, and intensity rating
1135.skill_description: Guide the client to identify and name current emotions, differentiate thoughts from emotions, assess intensity (e.g., 0–10 or percentage), and connect to automatic thought and behavior patterns; continuously monitor by recording current emotions and bodily sensations, emotion diaries, and reflection on causes, enhance emotional awareness and self-regulation ability.
1135.when_to_use: Initial assessment and education stages of counseling, or whenever intense emotions occur and a shift from chaotic experience to clear identification and quantification is needed.
1135.trigger: Client vaguely describes 'uncomfortable' or 'uneasy' without clear naming; significant anxiety/sadness due to others' tone or lack of response; confusion between thoughts and feelings, difficulty quantifying intensity.

861.skill_name: Teach and supervise relaxation training and home practice
861.skill_description: Teach and practice relaxation training on-site (e.g., breathing, muscle or imagery relaxation), arrange regular homework and follow-up review, reduce physiological arousal and tension anxiety, improve sleep, serve as a basis for entering cognitive work and consolidating emotional improvement.
861.when_to_use: Psychological help stage and later consolidation, or when noticeable anxiety, tension, or insomnia occurs, used to stabilize emotions beforehand.
861.trigger: Nervousness, anxiety, insomnia during class, restless or palpitations as physiological tension signals during sessions; expressing a need for self-regulation tools.

964.skill_description: Name and rate emotions such as anxiety/sadness on a scale of 0–100 or 0–10. When necessary, set target values and mark intensity as a percentage in the thought record. Re-evaluate before and after intervention to track changes, providing quantitative basis for cognitive reappraisal and behavioral intervention.
964.when_to_use: When setting consultation goals, in assessment and monitoring phases, or when documenting automatic thoughts and evaluations that require quantifying and tracking emotional changes.
964.trigger: When the client's emotional fluctuation is significant, and it is difficult to specify when/why they are more tense; reporting intense discomfort or 'mood worsening,' requiring visual tracking of data.

990.skill_name: Allowing and Facilitating Safe Emotional Release
990.skill_description: Allow and encourage expression of sadness and anger through crying, providing a accepting environment and time. Arrange an emotional release room when necessary for safe release; pause intervention when emotions are high, and resume after emotions stabilize to reduce immediate distress and restore function.
990.when_to_use: When strong emotional accumulation has affected learning and life, or when early emotional arousal during the session makes it difficult to focus.
990.trigger: Heartbreaking crying lasting for several hours with no motivation, long-term suppression difficult to relieve; crying and rigid silence unwilling to communicate when discussing traumatic experiences; impulses for expression or self-harm.

1094.skill_name: Implementing Relaxation Confrontation and Reappraisal Desensitization Training
1094.skill_description: Implement anxiety-relaxation training from low to high on the rating scale. Induce a relaxed state first before entering the situation, creating a relaxed environment. Cover 1–4 levels each time. Re-evaluate anxiety scores after practice. If the score is above the threshold (e.g., 25 points), continue relaxation until the score significantly decreases before moving to the next level.
1094.when_to_use: To enter the training phase after completing the rating scale, or when consolidating relaxation effects during training and preparing to transition to higher levels.
1094.trigger: Tension not relieved during training or high scores; preparing for a tension response in specific situations, needing relaxation confrontation of anxiety.

1093.skill_name: Constructing Anxiety Situation Rating Scale and Scoring
1093.skill_description: List events that trigger anxiety with the client according to situations, and rate the intensity of tension/anxiety for each item, forming a bottom-up rating scale, providing a clear sequence and hierarchy for systematic desensitization and emotional regulation training.
1093.when_to_use: When defining the gradient and sequence of training is needed before starting systematic desensitization or emotional training.
1093.trigger: Anxiety intensity differs under different cues (thoughts, encounters, conversations, etc.), making it difficult to cope with all at once, requiring phased progression.

1186.skill_name: Quantify and Track Emotional Change Assessment
1186.skill_description: Invite the client to rate their current or recent week's emotions using a scale (e.g., 0–10 or 0–100), re-measure before and after cognitive intervention, and compare the changes; summarize at stages and review the magnitude of decrease and methods used at the end, reinforcing self-monitoring and self-efficacy.
1186.when_to_use: Opening of the session, before and after each intervention, and at stage/ending phases, for process monitoring and effect evaluation.
1186.trigger: Client reports significant emotional changes or after completing an exercise/homework, requiring objective measurement of the magnitude of change; significant symptom fluctuation requires tracking.

1118.skill_name: Deep Breathing and Muscle Relaxation for Rapid Emotional Regulation
1118.skill_description: Guide slow, even deep breathing, focus on the breathing rhythm, and combine repeated practice of muscle tensing—releasing with positive self-talk (e.g., mature, brave, rational), to rapidly reduce sympathetic arousal, alleviate worry, anxiety, and fear, and restore control and an objective attitude toward emotions.
1118.when_to_use: When establishing an 'emotional fluctuation coping program' in the relapse prevention phase; self-practice during emotional elevation in exposure or daily stimulus situations, or before sleep or when tense.
1118.trigger: Anxiety signals such as palpitations, tension, rapid breathing, muscle tightness, or fear of eye contact, or facing a stimulus that evokes fear.

1059.skill_name: Demonstrate and Apply Relaxation Training to Reduce Tension
1059.skill_description: Briefly explain the principle and steps of progressive muscle relaxation or diaphragmatic breathing, demonstrate the muscle/breath or information breathing technique in session to allow the client to experience the difference between tension and relaxation; apply to rapidly reduce physiological activation before high-stress events or peak tension, creating a tolerable state for subsequent cognitive assessment and exposure.
1059.when_to_use: Stress relief segments in emotional monitoring, or when needing a stable state before exposure or peak tension to maintain the session and practice.
1059.trigger: Tension reactions such as insomnia, headache, tightness, fatigue, trembling, chest tightness; anticipation of a conflict/high-stress event.

868.skill_name: Provide Supportive Listening and Acceptance of Expression
868.skill_description: Create a relationship and space of acceptance through genuine listening and emotional response, allowing ample expression, crying, and silence, to alleviate immediate distress, promote entry into the heart, and build trust, paving the way for subsequent data collection, clarification of issues, and cognitive intervention.
868.when_to_use: Throughout, especially in the relationship building and emotional support stages, or when emotional loss of control during acute stress affects basic communication.
868.trigger: Long-term self-isolation and accumulated pain, crying anxiously in the middle of the night; continuous crying or stiff silence during sessions, actively expressing negative emotions and distress.

1194.skill_name: Assess and provide feedback on emotional changes using SAS/SDS scale
1194.skill_description: Administer SAS/SDS (SCL-90 if necessary) during initial, end, or stage reassessments to establish anxiety/depression baselines and record changes in scores before and after; explain and provide feedback on results on the spot to help clients objectively recognize the level of emotion and improvement, guiding subsequent interventions and self-regulation.
1194.when_to_use: During initial sessions to establish a baseline, at the end of a stage, or when assessing outcomes and providing feedback.
1194.trigger: Need to objectively understand the severity of anxiety/depression or verify the effectiveness of the intervention; client agrees to undergo psychological assessment.

1076.skill_name: Teach and practice progressive muscle relaxation
1076.skill_description: Guide the client to sequentially tense and relax head—neck—arm—shoulder—back—chest—abdomen—buttocks—thigh—leg—toes, coordinating with breathing to experience full relaxation; assign daily short exercises to reduce physiological arousal, alleviate tension, and difficulty sleeping; apply as necessary before and during exposure-reaction prevention to stabilize emotions.
1076.when_to_use: When anxiety is significant, sleep is disturbed, or when needing to stabilize pre-exam states; before and during exposure-reaction prevention.
1076.trigger: Somatic tension, difficulty sleeping, anxiety and repression, etc., psychosomatic reactions; difficulty controlling emotions and physical discomfort.

1029.skill_name: Name and rate emotions in thought records
1029.skill_description: Use a three-column/five-column form to clearly define the situation, automatic thoughts, emotion name, and intensity percentage, establishing a clear link between 'emotion—thought—behavior'; demonstrate in sessions and practice as homework repeatedly between sessions, as a baseline for subsequent rational responses and outcome assessment.
1029.when_to_use: During the phase of horizontal analysis and identification/assessment of automatic thoughts; systematic tracking of emotional changes during homework and consolidation periods.
1029.trigger: Client's emotional expression is vague or confuses emotions with facts, making it difficult to distinguish and quantify its intensity.

1023.skill_name: Teach and encourage diaphragmatic breathing practice
1023.skill_description: Demonstrate key points of diaphragmatic breathing: adopt a comfortable posture, inhale through the nose to fill the abdomen, brief pause, exhale slowly through the mouth; follow a rhythm of inhaling for 3–4 seconds, holding for 2 seconds, exhaling for 3–4 seconds, and associate it with the 'balloon deflation' imagery, focusing on the breathing rhythm; assign regular practice and review in follow-up, first for sleep, then transfer to emotional fluctuation scenarios to relieve irritability, tension, and insomnia.
1023.when_to_use: When emotional management and sleep disturbance coexist; late in the first consultation or when emotions are high, stress is high, or insomnia is evident.
1023.trigger: Irritability, tension, difficulty sleeping, high physiological arousal, rapid breathing, or physiological anxiety signals such as 'very panicked'.

1139.skill_name: Initial Assessment and Quantification of Emotional Intensity
1139.skill_description: Have the client clearly state their current core emotion and quantify it using 0–100% or 0–10 to establish a repeatable intensity baseline; re-assess before and after intervention, and quantify related belief certainty when necessary, to compare changes and guide subsequent technique selection.
1139.when_to_use: When establishing an emotional baseline to guide intervention and monitor effects at the start of a session or before thought records; to grasp intensity and trends when coordinating with interventions.
1139.trigger: Generalized descriptions such as "uncomfortable, anxious, depressed" without quantitative indicators; when reporting compulsive events or intense panic, or significant emotional fluctuations requiring rapid quantification.

911.skill_description: Guide the client to review the key points, feelings, and gains of the current or phase work in their own words, summarize changes and satisfaction in areas such as emotion, relationships, sleep, learning, and express their understanding and confusion about the changes. Use their subjective evaluation for effect assessment, plan adjustment, and decision-making for ending/follow-up, to consolidate motivation and consulting outcomes.
911.when_to_use: In the ending and consolidation phase or at the end of each session; for phase summaries, case closure evaluations, and feedback after follow-up.
911.trigger: When the client can describe and is willing to share recent experiences and changes, or has feelings about consulting effectiveness or homework and raises questions.

1037.skill_name: Collecting and Evaluating Feedback on Homework Effectiveness
1037.skill_description: Invite the client to report on the execution of the homework and their subjective experience, combining recorded data and life changes (such as screen time, sleep, learning, interpersonal mindset), to evaluate completion and effectiveness, identify difficulties and questions, as a basis for subsequent homework and plan adjustments.
1037.when_to_use: Before the end of a session or during phase reviews/follow-ups, to evaluate the effectiveness of homework and intervention.
1037.trigger: When the client has implemented or partially implemented homework, brought in recorded data, or reports changes/non-completion requiring evaluation.

999.skill_name: Collecting Feedback on Feasibility of Exercises and Homework
999.skill_description: At the end, ask the client to describe their experience, difficulties, and feasibility of the new method/homework (e.g., initially unaccustomed but willing to persist), and supplement with specific behaviors and changes, to evaluate acceptance and fine-tune strategies and subsequent arrangements.
999.when_to_use: Before the end of a session reviewing homework or after the implementation of a new strategy, or during phase reviews.
999.trigger: When homework/record/behavior experiments have been attempted, expressing discomfort, doubts, willingness to persist, or being able to describe specific experiences.

873.skill_description: After key technical explanations/exercises or the session topic concludes, invite the visitor to provide immediate feedback on their current feelings, understanding, and adaptability, receive emotional responses, respond to questions, record key points, and provide a basis for summary and plan adjustment.
873.when_to_use: After completing an operation, topic, or important exercise, and during the feedback phase at the end of a session.
873.trigger: Emotional/behavioral reactions such as relaxation or crying; or when confusion, or significant feelings about the consultation process and style are expressed.

1124.skill_name: Guide self-assessment of consultation effect and changes
1124.skill_description: Ask the visitor to describe their current situation and changes (such as mood, sleep, appetite, confidence, etc.) and future plans, using their subjective evaluation as feedback to examine efficacy and appropriately reinforce effective practices or arrange for continued use.
1124.when_to_use: At the end of a consultation or during a phase assessment, or during the overall review at the end of each session.
1124.trigger: The visitor proactively or upon invitation reports changes such as 'sleep is better, I have more confidence,' and proposes continuation and plans.

1172.skill_name: Collect satisfaction and remaining concerns to adjust the plan
1172.skill_description: Inquire about satisfaction with the consultation effect and remaining concerns, encourage the expression of unresolved questions and difficulties (including homework), and adjust the next topic and intervention intensity accordingly, maintaining congruence and engagement.
1172.when_to_use: At the end of a session, during a phase assessment, or during follow-up, to plan future directions.
1172.trigger: Approaching the end requiring a focus decision; when the visitor mentions unease, confusion, or residual anxiety points in their feedback.

1024.skill_name: Collect overall satisfaction and suggestions at termination
1024.skill_description: In the termination/post-session follow-up phase, invite the visitor (and family) to provide feedback on their satisfaction, experience, and suggestions regarding the intervention plan and the entire treatment process, collect self-report and other-report changes and concerns, as a basis for consolidation and future support.
1024.when_to_use: After intervention completion, at the end of a course, follow-up after a consultation phase, and the final part of the session.
1024.trigger: Need to systematically understand the overall experience and effect; when the visitor reports satisfaction or provides suggestions and future plans.

1038.skill_name: Processing feelings related to the end and negotiating follow-up plans
1038.skill_description: Discussing and receiving emotions and questions related to the ending when nearing the end, reviewing failures and difficulties, negotiating next steps and support resources based on feedback, helping with a smooth transition, reducing anxiety, and sustaining change.
1038.when_to_use: The tail end of the assessment/ending phase, especially in termination conversations or phase-endings.
1038.trigger: Expressing anxiety, attachment, or questions about the end; hesitation/delay in task execution; expressing a desire to continue practicing and discussing.

885.skill_name: Inviting sharing of gains, feelings, and confusion from this session
885.skill_description: Inviting the client to share their gains and feelings from this session or phase in their own words, and allowing for self-rating, supplementing subjective experiences such as emotions/spirit and remaining troubles, to provide information for adjusting subsequent topics and consolidating motivation.
885.when_to_use: Consolidation/summary phase before the end of the session, or after phase review and re-testing.
885.trigger: The session is about to end; the client reports experiences such as relaxation, joy, or sudden clarity, or needs to supplement subjective impact.

1022.skill_name: Reviewing the path and methods of change
1022.skill_description: Guiding the client to review how the change occurred, restating key ideas and practice paths (such as rational thinking and practice), clarifying the understanding of the process, and consolidating the grasp of the mechanism and self-replication ability.
1022.when_to_use: In end feedback, ensuring the method is understood and can be used independently.
1022.trigger: The client has reported change, but the understanding of the process and key points remains vague.

874.skill_name: Affirming positive changes and reinforcing sustained motivation
874.skill_description: Giving appropriate affirmation and encouragement based on the client's progress and success experiences, evoking positive emotions, enhancing self-efficacy and the desire to continue trying, paving the way for subsequent tasks and behavior maintenance.
874.when_to_use: In session feedback/termination, or after completing challenging practices and tasks.
874.trigger: Reporting positive changes such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, application of rational thinking, or completing a task but uncertainty about the outcome.

1075.skill_name: Feedback on Assignment/Exercise Completion and Experience
1075.skill_description: Ask the client to report on the frequency of assignment or exercise execution, specific experiences, and insights gained, organize difficulties and areas for improvement, to serve as a basis for adjusting subsequent arrangements and support strategies.
1075.when_to_use: During scheduled feedback times related to the consultation or after the exercise concludes, in the feedback segment before the session ends.
1075.trigger: When the client is willing to share the execution experience and specific changes during the assignment cycle or exercise completion.

969.skill_name: Receiving Negative Feedback and Providing Explanation and Clarification
969.skill_description: Proactively invite and receive discomfort and negative feedback, promptly explain the process and purpose regarding complaints/doubts, and provide necessary psychoeducation and clarification to repair the relationship and promote continued cooperation and assignment execution.
969.when_to_use: During the feedback segment before each session, used for collecting experiences and issues.
969.trigger: When the client expresses disappointment, anxiety, complaints, or doubts about the treatment and assignment.

905.skill_name: Checking Assignments and Inviting Sharing of Changes
905.skill_description: During assignment checking, invite the client to share their experiences and insights gained from the assignment and consultation, inquire about feelings and interpersonal/life changes within a week, receive feedback on completion status, to serve as a basis for further exploration and adjustment.
905.when_to_use: During the concluding and consolidation phase or the feedback segment at the start of the next session; for phase summaries and follow-ups.
905.trigger: When the client brings completed assignments and submits/reports verbally; when the client attends on time and experiences related changes within a week, or has new insights after a group course.

983.skill_name: Listing and Weighing For and Against Evidence
983.skill_description: Around the current belief, ask item by item for specific facts and situations that support and oppose it, compare the sufficiency and reliability of the evidence, identify overgeneralization and inference from a single source, use counterexamples to loosen the entire conclusion, and reduce the certainty of old beliefs.
983.when_to_use: When evaluating intermediate beliefs or strong automatic thoughts, or preparing to challenge unreasonable beliefs; when the client draws a stable conclusion based on fragmented experiences or single information.
983.trigger: When the client insists on judgments like "all/must/only" or conclusions like "she will ruin me," based on vague, ignoring contrary facts, and accompanied by anxiety, anger, or shame.

930.skill_name: Perspective-Taking to Generate Counter-Evidence and Explanations
930.skill_description: Invite the client to speculate on the intent and feelings from another's perspective, and generate alternative explanations and counter-examples using questions such as "What would you say if a friend were in this situation?" to expose and test one's own assumptions, weaken single explanations and overgeneralization.
930.when_to_use: When interpersonal conflict or single negative attribution of others' motives occurs, expand the perspective, seek counter-evidence, and more understandable explanations.
930.trigger: Insisting on assertions like "She doesn't care about me/They don't welcome me," refusing to stand in the other person's shoes, emotional agitation, or providing only one-sided evidence.

1069.skill_description: Shift vague judgments from "facts" to "thoughts," question the basis and source, list supporting and opposing evidence item by item, verify external information and review for any related attempts and outcomes, identify biases, and reduce certainty.
1069.when_to_use: When the client adheres to a certain belief and is significantly affected by it, or when relying on vague or single sources.
1069.trigger: Asserting in a positive tone like "They don't like me/I am not good enough," lacking specific examples of support, or treating others' views as facts.

955.skill_name: Reassessing Feasibility Based on New Information
955.skill_description: After clarifying evidence and alternative explanations emerge, ask "Do you think there is still a possibility to continue now?" to promote integrated judgment, update conclusions, and point toward real choices, further reducing certainty about old beliefs.
955.when_to_use: When promoting conclusion integration and decision clarification after evidence verification.
955.trigger: The client admits other reasons but remains undecided, has difficulty reaching a conclusion, or persistently fixates on the old situation.

870.skill_name: Collecting Balanced Evidence of Pros and Cons
870.skill_description: Guide the recall of contrary facts and positive feedback, verify evidence sources, incorporate past successes and objective information, use factual counter-examples to challenge absolute labels, balance single negative evidence, and reduce the certainty of "universal denial."
870.when_to_use: When the client supports universal denial with a single negative event or subjective conjecture, expand the sample and incorporate positive evidence.
870.trigger: Only citing negative evaluations, using absolute terms like "all/always/definitely," or insisting on "I am a failure/incompetent.

949.skill_description: After a round of evidence comparison, invite the client to self-rate the reasonableness and naming bias of their thoughts (such as "too absolute"), to consolidate the nascent sprouts of new ideas, and promote spontaneous correction rather than added persuasion.
949.when_to_use: When the client shows cognitive loosening and is able to consider alternative explanations, use it to consolidate the direction of correction.
949.trigger: Expressing signs of wavering such as "seems/maybe/possibly too absolute," and willingness to reflect on original rules.

900.skill_description: Use heuristic questioning to transform vague emotions into statementable sentences, focusing on listing unreasonable beliefs such as catastrophizing or absolutization (such as "must... otherwise total failure"), to lay the groundwork for subsequent testing and correction with objects and material.
900.when_to_use: When entering cognitive intervention after establishing a relationship, and preparing to assess anxiety-related concepts.
900.trigger: Repeatedly expressing extreme statements such as "terrible," "people look down on me," or erroneous attribution.

1177.skill_name: Clarifying event sequence and objective information
1177.skill_description: Ask the client to specifically recall and clarify the event sequence and background, stripping away speculation and evaluation, first establishing a clear, verifiable factual basis, to provide a basis for subsequent examination and debate of unreasonable beliefs.
1177.when_to_use: At the beginning of the stage of correcting unreasonable beliefs, or when a one-sided narrative is used to support a conclusion.
1177.trigger: Attributing blame with vague, inferential language (such as "it's all because of me"), without explaining the factual sequence and details.

1195.skill_name: Counter-example and possibility questioning to weaken necessity
1195.skill_description: Question assertions of "must/all/certainty," invite the search for exceptions and uncertain factors, review contrary results and potential helpers, using counter-examples to shake excessive generalizations and catastrophizing inferences, reducing rigid conclusions driven by anxiety.
1195.when_to_use: When the client universalizes a single experience, or when there are necessary inferences such as "others must be better/I definitely won't pass".
1195.trigger: Using words such as "all/must/only" or statements such as "no one cares" or "it will definitely be bad".

1117.skill_name: Making the Situation and Observable Examples Concrete
1117.skill_description: Guide the client to specifically describe the roles, tasks, and behavioral details in the current situation, and explore the subsequent plot if the belief were true, selecting 1-2 verifiable events to ground abstract evaluations, facilitating subsequent evidence testing and assessment.
1117.when_to_use: When moving from generalized statements to observable events, or in the early stages of assessing intermediate beliefs.
1117.trigger: Only vague descriptions such as "very uncomfortable/afraid" are used, lacking specific examples or inability to locate the key situation and behavior.

923.skill_name: Clarifying Event-Belief-Outcome using the ABC Model
923.skill_description: Clearly distinguish and record the precipitating event A, the belief B, and the consequence C; use a table for comparison when necessary to prompt the client to shift from the event to examining the belief, clarifying the source of the emotion, and laying the foundation for subsequent debate and modification.
923.when_to_use: When assessing the source of emotional distress, preparing to question unreasonable beliefs, or in the stage of introducing ABC and beginning to organize.
923.trigger: Attributing negative emotions directly to external events, or the appearance of absolutistic thoughts such as "should/shame/once".

1102.skill_description: Invite the client to rate key beliefs and emotions with scores or percentages to establish a comparable baseline; re-score after evidence testing and discussion, observe changes, and reinforce rational assessment and self-monitoring.
1102.when_to_use: When examining a disbelieving belief before and after, or after completing a round of discussion to assess intensity changes and intervention effects.
1102.trigger: Holding high certainty in beliefs such as "I am helpless/I am a failure," or when emotions are clearly relieved and preparing for re-evaluation.

920.skill_name: Identifying Cognitive Distortions and Attempting Reappraisal
920.skill_description: Use heuristic questions to invite self-assessment of catastrophizing, absolutizing, etc., and attempt to view from different angles, helping to detach from extreme inferences and unfounded predictions, reducing the subjective certainty and emotional drive of the original belief.
920.when_to_use: When the client has stated specific thoughts or exhibits rigid negative interpretations, or when emotions are high.
920.trigger: Statements containing necessity and extreme conclusions (e.g., "the cat will bite me/I am definitely going to be attacked") or admitting to thinking only of the worst outcome.

919.skill_name: Retrospective Context Identification of Automatic Thinking
919.skill_description: Using the most recent triggered event as a clue, reconstruct the situation and details at that time, articulate the thoughts/images in sequence, and distinguish between thoughts and facts, clarify the trigger clue, providing actionable objects for subsequent recording, examination, and correction.
919.when_to_use: When beginning to process a specific triggered event, or reviewing segments of conversations about recent coercive/anxiety experiences.
919.trigger: Reporting strong emotions and bodily reactions, repeatedly recalling events but not clearly expressing their views and assumptions.

924.skill_name: Perspective Taking to Test Interpersonal Assumptions
924.skill_description: Through role-swapping and hypothetical situations, imagine the other person's position, feelings, and circumstances, examine the impact of one's own behavior on others, generate alternative explanations, reduce one-sided attribution and interpersonal tension.
924.when_to_use: When discussing interpersonal conflict or worries about being excluded, the client insists on a single perspective and has difficulty understanding others' reactions.
924.trigger: Only emphasizing the other person's fault, asserting negative motives, fear of communication, or not proactively participating in discussions or activities.

903.skill_name: Systematic Review of Growth History, Family Interactions, and Key Events
903.skill_description: Guide the client to review major life events and turning points according to a timeline or developmental stage, record the emotions and coping mechanisms at that time, systematically collect information on upbringing in the native family, expectations and evaluations of important others, academic trajectory, and traumatic experiences, organize the narrative of person—situation—and timeline, laying the groundwork of data for locating the source and maintenance clues of negative core beliefs.
903.when_to_use: When systematically understanding the growth history and coping patterns is needed during the phase of establishing a relationship or evaluating and conceptualizing the case or core beliefs.
903.trigger: When the client mentions childhood upbringing, being compared/neglected, family changes, academic fluctuations, or traumatic experiences; or when confused about the cause of a problem.

1198.skill_name: Linking Early Experiences with Current Beliefs and Behavior Chains
1198.skill_description: Based on the growth narrative, link "event—interpretation—emotion—behavior," combine important others' expectations and evaluations, string together experience chains such as "lack of warmth→distrust/fear→sensitive inferiority→desire and avoidance," connect with current interpersonal rules, automatic thoughts, and avoidance strategies, reconstruct the formation and maintenance mechanism of negative core beliefs, and provide feedback.
1198.when_to_use: After collecting growth history data, during the phase of core belief evaluation and case conceptualization, when locating the source and maintenance mechanism of beliefs is needed.
1198.trigger: When the client narrates being overly cared for/compared, long-term avoidance of interaction, experiencing family changes, specific trauma, and self-statements such as "I am not good enough/I cannot change".

840.skill_name: Integrate current distress and early experiences to propose core belief hypotheses
840.skill_description: Integrate current material such as depression and self-blame stemming from academic setbacks with childhood experiences such as being hit, compared, or neglected, annotate the formation and activation contexts of core beliefs like "incompetent/worthless/neglected" along a timeline, and refine belief hypotheses that span multiple contexts to serve as targets for subsequent evaluation and modification.
840.when_to_use: When case material is sufficient, in the information gathering and case conceptualization stage, or when entering the third stage to prepare for belief work.
840.trigger: When the client repeatedly presents global self-evaluations such as "I am bad/I can't do anything" in different contexts, or expresses that they always react similarly in similar situations.

1070.skill_name: Trace childhood and parenting experiences to collect belief evidence
1070.skill_description: Review key childhood and adolescent events and important others' reactions according to developmental history, detail episodes of corporal punishment, humiliation, neglect, attachment/bullying, record thoughts and emotions at the time, systematically organize parental expectations and social comparison cues, to serve as specific evidence for the origins of core beliefs such as "I am not worthy of love/nobody likes me".
1070.when_to_use: In the initial stage of case conceptualization and core belief evaluation, when tracing early negative experiences and establishing the path and evidence base is necessary.
1070.trigger: When the client mentions experiences of being denied/compared, strict corporal punishment by parents or little companionship, humiliation by teachers, long-term loneliness, and interpersonal conflicts.

1098.skill_name: Collect growth history and multi-source information from important others
1098.skill_description: Based on registration forms, initial interviews, and observations, structure questions and record information about family members and educational background, parenting styles and expectations, family economic status, personality and social interaction history, academic performance; gather statements from important others such as mothers/uncles/teachers to corroborate and correct, form a clear developmental history, support the analysis of formation pathways.
1098.when_to_use: In the initial assessment and diagnosis stage of counseling, or before case conceptualization/core belief evaluation when a complete developmental history needs to be established.
1098.trigger: When the client provides clues about family background and childhood experiences, or states that they are limited/negative and need others to supplement; when the initial interview is accompanied by intense emotions and symptom narration.

1106.skill_name: Systematically understand growth experiences and current status in the first session
1106.skill_description: In the diagnostic assessment of the first session, systematically collect information about family and growth experiences, parent-child interactions and important events, learning and interpersonal status and functional impairment, and interview important others such as mothers or teachers when necessary, to clarify the root of the problem and belief background, providing a basis for subsequent interventions (such as Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy).
1106.when_to_use: In the assessment and relationship building stage of the first session, preparing to enter belief evaluation or intervention.
1106.trigger: When the client experiences low mood, insomnia, decreased interest, interpersonal tension, or learning impairment in the past month, and mentions growth information such as parental demands/teacher advice.

846.skill_name: Sorting the Influence of Important Others' Expectations and Evaluations
846.skill_description: Focusing on the expectations and evaluations of important others such as parents and teachers, and family role preferences (such as son preference/daughter preference), punishment and conflict, comparing internal and external standards, analyzing how these interactions and social comparisons shape cognitive patterns such as "unliked/untrustworthy/not good enough," as causes and key threads for maintaining core beliefs.
846.when_to_use: When evaluating the impact of the expectations and evaluations of important others on core beliefs, or when biographical analysis focuses on family and school relationship excerpts.
846.trigger: When the client talks about high expectations/strictness/preferences from parents, high hopes from teachers, being compared and criticized, or worrying about failing expectations.

1188.skill_description: Based on collected growth experiences, evaluations from important others, and current automatic thoughts, emotions, and behavioral evidence, draw a conceptual structure map of the belief system or conceptual structure of self/others/world (including core and intermediate beliefs), visually presenting the formation and maintenance pathways of themes such as "world is unsafe," to facilitate verification, revision, and focusing subsequent interventions with the client.
1188.when_to_use: After completing data collection in the core belief evaluation stage, or during case conceptualization summary and feedback.
1188.trigger: When cross-period data is rich, thematic clues are clear (e.g., low sense of safety), and visualization and joint confirmation are needed.

1040.skill_name: Identifying Social Comparison and Its Effect on Beliefs
1040.skill_description: Reviewing cues of comparison with peers and teachers after entering a new environment (background/clothing/expression, changes in status and attention, differences in position, etc.), recording relevant others' evaluations and emotional reactions, analyzing the inference chain from comparison to "inferior everywhere/being labeled/not being understood," and linking these A events with emotional/behavioral C manifestations, clarifying their reinforcing effect on core beliefs.
1040.when_to_use: When assessing the evidence base and rationality of core beliefs, or sorting the influence of social comparison and others' evaluations.
1040.trigger: When the client mentions comparison with peers, changes in position, inferiority, or being labeled, or when support decreases in unfamiliar environments.

1073.skill_name: Recognizing the Maintaining Role of Personality and Coping Styles
1073.skill_description: Summarizing personality tendencies such as introversion, competitiveness/cowardice, poor emotional control, and coping styles such as avoidance, withdrawal, endurance, prioritizing others' needs, identifying how defenses like repetitive cleaning and avoiding going out are negatively reinforced, linking them to automatic thoughts and core beliefs such as "surroundings are unsafe," as a basis for symptom persistence and intervention priority.
1073.when_to_use: When core beliefs have been preliminarily clarified or a case conceptualization has been built, used to identify maintaining factors and plan intervention targets.
1073.trigger: When the client has less proactive contact, avoids conflict, finds it difficult to ask for help, only evaluates themselves by grades, or exhibits behaviors such as compulsive cleaning, fear of sleeping alone, or not going out at night.

883.skill_name: Inquisitive Talk to Collect Growth History and Support Information
883.skill_description: In inquisitive talk and assessment, systematically collect demographic information, family background, personal growth history, and school support information, combined with record forms and observation/probe of introversion, perfectionism, learning setbacks, and other personality traits and experiences, to make preliminary judgments on problem attribution clues and core belief causes, laying the foundation for subsequent analysis and intervention.
883.when_to_use: During the assessment, diagnosis, and relationship-building phase of the first consultation, or when conducting problem attribution analysis.
883.trigger: When the client experiences relationship tension in the dormitory accompanied by anxiety, depression, insomnia, and loneliness; or when experiencing mid-term setbacks, clear perfectionistic demands, and unclear understanding of the problem's origin and progression.

1084.skill_name: Locating Specific Situations and Mining Automatic Thoughts and Reactions
1084.skill_description: Guide the client to review specific events or current stimulus situations from the past week, using prompting questions such as "What am I thinking when my emotions change?" to timely mine the automatic thoughts that arose at that time, and confirm the accompanying emotions, behaviors/physiological reactions, forming monitoring material in the pattern of situation—thought—emotion—behavior, to lay the groundwork for subsequent recording and assessment.
1084.when_to_use: In the initial stage of learning to identify automatic thoughts and at the beginning of the session; when monitoring specific triggering situations encountered in the past or daily, to collect and locate recording material.
1084.trigger: When the client vaguely describes distress or reports events such as exam failure, unreturned interpersonal interactions, or sudden contact, followed by physical and mental reactions such as anxiety, sadness, panic, avoidance, insomnia, etc., requiring backtracking to the current thoughts.

934.skill_name: Timely Recording of Situation—Automatic Thought—Emotion and Scoring
934.skill_description: As per assignment requirements, record the situation, automatic thought, and emotion/behavior as soon as possible after the event occurred, and subjectively score the intensity of the emotion, continuously observe intensity changes, identify typical high-frequency situations and related thought clues, as foundational data for subsequent testing and re-evaluation.
934.when_to_use: During the stage of learning to identify automatic thoughts and in weekly homework; fill out as soon as possible, either immediately after the event or afterward, when experiencing negative emotions or significant fluctuations.
934.trigger: When experiencing negative emotions such as sadness, anxiety, or disappointment, or when encountering stimuli such as receiving a text message, worrying about being talked about, or learning setbacks, accompanied by intense emotional/physiological reactions, rumination, or escape.

1152.skill_name: Recording and Reflecting by ABC/Event-Emotion-Thought-Behavior Structure
1152.skill_description: Use a brief record form or the ABC framework to clarify the precipitating event (A), the emotion and behavioral manifestation at that time (C), and the automatic/irrational belief (B) within it, and record the event—emotion—thought—behavior in sequence; can track emotional states across multiple time points, and after completion, briefly write down the thought "Why is it like this?" to continuously monitor and provide feedback on changes, establishing a baseline of emotion—trigger.
1152.when_to_use: Homework after the identification stage following psychological diagnosis and insight/initial assessment; when experiencing anxiety, restlessness, worry about academics, interpersonal relationships, or the future daily or before sleep, or when needing to review after a conflict occurs.
1152.trigger: When the client can describe specific events and report emotional distress; when experiencing emotional fluctuations, sleep changes, social avoidance, or physical discomfort; when noticing experiences such as anger, sadness, anxiety, or related automatic thoughts; when difficulty recalling immediate thoughts and feelings during a conflict.

1166.skill_name: Review and record recent distressing events, emotions, and thoughts
1166.skill_description: Review experiences such as anxiety, low mood, insomnia, and thoughts from a recent period according to the assignment requirements, record recent distressing events item by item; fill out an emotion management chart weekly and record daily emotional fluctuations and negative behaviors; when there are many items, select the most intense typical event as a starting point to focus and improve the efficiency of subsequent processing.
1166.when_to_use: Start collecting materials for homework after the first consultation; determine the primary target event when monitoring or organizing recent distressing items; used for reviewing a week's emotions and behaviors before subsequent weekly sessions.
1166.trigger: Ability to recall emotional fluctuations and corresponding thoughts from a recent period; being repeatedly troubled by an event recently; experiencing low mood or negative behaviors; when listing multiple worries makes it difficult to focus or choose a starting point.

1111.skill_name: Review and refine records and explore clues during sessions
1111.skill_description: Discuss the client's event and emotion records item by item during the session, verify details and completeness; clarify and probe around the recorded clues, specify and record emotions and behaviors/physiological reactions in the C section, quantify the impact of distress; systematically review the intensity of emotions and monitoring items from a week, as an entry point for deeper understanding and revision.
1111.when_to_use: When reviewing homework at the second consultation; for subsequent follow-ups, deepen understanding and revise based on records; when the session begins or transitions to the middle part to receive homework and enter the current topic, or when quantifying the impact of distress is needed.
1111.trigger: Client brings records or verbalizes a week's emotional fluctuations, records have gaps, ambiguities, or suggest potential deeper conflicts; mentions obvious low mood, physical discomfort, or functional impairment (learning stagnation, skipping classes, etc).

941.skill_name: Use a three-column chart to record situation—automatic thought—emotion and supplement reaction and rating
941.skill_description: As soon as possible, in the moment or after, use a three-column chart to list the situation, automatic thought, and emotion, practice accurate naming and subjective rating; simultaneously supplement bodily/behavioral reactions, classify situations with high emotions by type when necessary, help clarify the cognitive—emotion—behavior relationship, continuously capture and identify automatic thoughts.
